has_subtypes:
- name: MYCN-Amplified Neuroblastoma
  classification: molecular
  description: >-
    Approximately 20% of neuroblastomas harbor MYCN gene amplification,
    associated with rapid tumor progression and poor prognosis. MYCN
    amplification is one of the earliest oncogene amplifications discovered.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41560679
    reference_title: "Coexpression of MYCN and ALK Induces Neuroblastoma-Like Tumors From Human iPS Cell-Derived Cranial Neural Crest Cells."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "MYCN amplification is a key factor contributing to the poor prognosis of NB."
    explanation: >-
      States the adverse prognostic association of MYCN amplification. The
      sentence is background in the abstract of an iPSC-derived neural crest
      model study, restating the clinical picture; it is not something that
      study measured. The patient-derived support is the Brodeur and INRG
      evidence below.
  - reference: PMID:6719137
    reference_title: "Amplification of N-myc in untreated human neuroblastomas correlates with advanced disease stage."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Furthermore, N-myc amplification is highly correlated with advanced stages of disease (P less than 0.001) and with the ability to grow in vitro as an established cell line, both of which are associated with a poor prognosis."
    explanation: >-
      Human clinical support for the rapid-progression and poor-prognosis
      claim, from untreated primary neuroblastoma tissue.
  - reference: PMID:19047291
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) classification system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Stage, age, histologic category, grade of tumor differentiation, the status of the MYCN oncogene, chromosome 11q status, and DNA ploidy were the most highly statistically significant and clinically relevant factors."
    explanation: >-
      Confirms MYCN status as a statistically significant, clinically relevant
      prognostic factor in the 8,800-patient INRG cohort.
  - reference: PMID:22936790
    reference_title: "N-myc and noncoding RNAs in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Amplification and overexpression of the MYCN proto-oncogene occurs in approximately 20% of neuroblastomas and is associated with advanced stage disease, rapid tumor progression, and poor prognosis."
    explanation: >-
      A review statement that amplification and overexpression of MYCN occur
      in approximately 20% of neuroblastomas and are associated with advanced
      stage disease, rapid tumor progression and poor prognosis, matching this
      subtype's description. The sentence pairs amplification with
      overexpression; it is read here as a statement about amplification.
- name: High-Risk Neuroblastoma
  classification: risk_group
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: high-risk neuroblastoma
    term:
      id: NCIT:C150281
      label: High Risk Neuroblastoma
  description: >-
    A pretreatment risk group that sets treatment intensity, not a histologic or
    molecular entity; which tumors it contains depends on the classification
    system. In the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) classification
    (2009), which defines 16 pretreatment groups, high risk denotes the groups
    with 5-year event-free survival below 50%, and 18 months was selected as the
    age cutoff. The Children's Oncology Group (COG) classifier version 2 (2021)
    uses the INRG Staging System (INRGSS) and adds segmental chromosome
    aberrations. Among stage L1, L2 and M tumors, it classifies as high risk
    stage M at 18 months or older, MYCN-amplified stage M at any age and stage M
    in toddlers aged 12 to under 18 months with any unfavorable biomarker, as
    well as MYCN-amplified L2 tumors, L2 tumors without MYCN amplification but
    with unfavorable International Neuroblastoma Pathology Classification (INPC)
    histology at 18 months or older, and incompletely resected MYCN-amplified L1
    tumors. Its rules for stage MS are set out separately; for stages M and MS
    together, MYCN status affected risk group assignment in children younger
    than 12 months, and MYCN status, histology, ploidy and segmental chromosome
    aberrations did so at 12 to 18 months. The International Society of
    Pediatric Oncology European Neuroblastoma Group (SIOPEN) high-risk trial
    HR-NBL1 took patients older than 12 months with International Neuroblastoma
    Staging System (INSS) stage 4 disease and patients with MYCN-amplified stage
    2, 3 or 4 disease. In the SIOPEN HR-NBL1.5 study, random assignment between
    two induction regimens used a 1-year age threshold: it was open to patients
    aged 1 to 20 years with stage 4 disease and to infants younger than 1 year
    with MYCN-amplified stage 4 or 4S disease. High-risk treatment typically
    includes myeloablative therapy and immunotherapy.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:19047291
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) classification system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The optimal age cutoff was determined to be between 15 and 19 months, and 18 months was selected for the classification system. Sixteen pretreatment groups were defined on the basis of clinical criteria and statistically significantly different EFS of the cohort stratified by the INRG criteria. Patients with 5-year EFS more than 85%, more than 75% to < or = 85%, > or = 50% to < or = 75%, or less than 50% were classified as very low risk, low risk, intermediate risk, or high risk, respectively."
    explanation: >-
      The INRG Task Force report found the optimal age cutoff to lie between 15
      and 19 months, and the Task Force selected 18 months for the
      classification system. In its cohort of 8,800 children diagnosed in
      1990-2002, sixteen pretreatment groups were defined, and groups with
      5-year event-free survival below 50% were classified as high risk. The
      risk categories are survival bands from this pooled cohort.
  - reference: PMID:34319759
    reference_title: "Revised Neuroblastoma Risk Classification System: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "A revised 2021 COG neuroblastoma risk classifier (version 2) that uses the INRGSS and incorporates SCAs has been adopted to prospectively define COG clinical trial eligibility and treatment assignment."
    explanation: >-
      The conclusion of this COG analysis of 4,832 patients on the ANBL00B1
      biology study states that the revised 2021 COG classifier (version 2) uses
      the INRGSS, incorporates segmental chromosome aberrations and has been
      adopted to define COG trial eligibility and treatment assignment. High
      risk is one of the groups this classifier assigns; the paper notes that
      risk schemas differ across cooperative groups.
  - reference: PMID:34319759
    reference_title: "Revised Neuroblastoma Risk Classification System: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Thus, L1 tumors are classified in v2 as LR except rare MYCN-A tumors (4%) that are incompletely resected (macroscopic residual tumor), which are considered HR. ... INPC was prognostic for most L2 subsets, with the largest impact in patients age >= 18 months with MYCN-NA tumors ... In this group, those with unfavorable INPC tumors had outcomes inferior to those with favorable or unknown INPC ... Thus, these patients, in addition to L2 patients with MYCN-A, are classified HR in v2."
    explanation: >-
      The results of the COG ANBL00B1 analysis state the three locoregional
      groups that COG version 2 classifies as high risk: incompletely resected
      MYCN-amplified L1 tumors, MYCN-amplified L2 tumors, and MYCN-non-amplified
      L2 tumors with unfavorable INPC histology in patients aged 18 months or
      older ("these patients" refers back to that subset). These are
      COG-specific rules.
  - reference: PMID:34319759
    reference_title: "Revised Neuroblastoma Risk Classification System: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The majority of patients with stage M disease are >= 18 months at diagnosis and their outcome remains poor (EFS and OS: 46.1% +/- 1.6% and 59.4% +/- 1.5%). ... Similarly, patients with stage M disease of any age with MYCN-A tumors have poor outcomes (EFS and OS: 44.5% +/- 2.3% and 51.0% +/- 2.3%). Both groups receive treatment that typically includes one or more myeloablative therapies10,26 and immunotherapy12,13 and remain HR in v2. ... Patients age 12 to < 18 months with INRGSS M disease had outcomes intermediate to those of patients age < 12 and >= 18 months. ... Thus, toddlers with stage M disease with any unfavorable biomarker are classified as HR in v2."
    explanation: >-
      In the COG ANBL00B1 cohort used to build the 2021 version 2 classifier,
      stage M disease at 18 months or older and MYCN-amplified stage M disease
      at any age had poor outcomes and remain high risk. The quote also gives
      the stage M group aged 12 to under 18 months, the source's toddlers, whose
      outcomes were intermediate, and states that toddlers with stage M disease
      and any unfavorable biomarker are classified high risk. The treatment
      clause describes standard high-risk therapy cited to earlier COG trials,
      not a finding of this analysis.
  - reference: PMID:34319759
    reference_title: "Revised Neuroblastoma Risk Classification System: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "For patients with stage M (metastatic) and MS (metastatic, special) disease, genomic biomarkers affected risk group assignment for those < 12 months (MYCN) or 12-18 months (MYCN, histology, ploidy, and SCA) of age. ... Risk classification for MS in v2 is discussed in the Data Supplement."
    explanation: >-
      The abstract of this COG ANBL00B1 analysis states that, for stages M and
      MS together, MYCN status affected risk group assignment under the revised
      classifier in children younger than 12 months, and MYCN status, histology,
      ploidy and segmental chromosome aberrations did so at 12 to 18 months. The
      sentence pools the two stages and does not say which stage MS groups are
      high risk; the results section refers stage MS risk classification under
      version 2 to the Data Supplement.
  - reference: PMID:30754710
    reference_title: "The Evolution of Risk Classification for Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Finally, SIOPEN completed a SIOPEN HR-NBL1 evaluating patients over 12 months with INSS stage 4 disease and patients with stage 2, 3, or 4 disease with MYCN amplification"
    explanation: >-
      This review of cooperative-group risk classification describes the SIOPEN
      high-risk trial HR-NBL1 as taking patients older than 12 months with INSS
      stage 4 disease and patients with MYCN-amplified stage 2, 3 or 4 disease,
      so its high-risk population included locoregional MYCN-amplified disease
      as well as metastatic disease. The review restates the trial's criteria
      and reports no patient data.
  - reference: PMID:34152804
    reference_title: "Randomized Trial of Two Induction Therapy Regimens for High-Risk Neuroblastoma: HR-NBL1.5 International Society of Pediatric Oncology European Neuroblastoma Group Study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Patients (age 1-20 years) with stage 4 neuroblastoma or stage 4/4s aged < 1 year with MYCN amplification were eligible for random assignment to rCOJEC or MSKCC-N5."
    explanation: >-
      States who was eligible for the HR-NBL1.5 randomization between two
      induction regimens: patients aged 1 to 20 years with stage 4
      neuroblastoma, or infants younger than 1 year with MYCN-amplified stage 4
      or 4S disease. The age threshold for stage 4 disease was therefore 1 year.
      This is eligibility for one randomization within a SIOPEN high-risk study,
      not the study's whole population or a SIOPEN definition of high risk.
- name: Adrenal Gland Neuroblastoma
  classification: anatomic
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: adrenal gland neuroblastoma
    term:
      id: MONDO:0006076
      label: adrenal gland neuroblastoma
  locations:
  - preferred_term: adrenal gland
    term:
      id: UBERON:0002369
      label: adrenal gland
  description: >-
    Neuroblastoma whose primary tumor arises in the adrenal gland. In the INRG
    database, 47% of 8,369 children with neuroblastoma or ganglioneuroblastoma
    and a known primary site had adrenal tumors. After adjustment for age, stage
    and histologic grade, adrenal primaries had about twice the odds of MYCN
    amplification of non-adrenal primaries (adjusted odds ratio 2.09), and after
    adjustment for age, MYCN status and stage they carried a modestly higher
    risk of events (hazard ratio 1.13).
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25154816
    reference_title: "Clinical, biologic, and prognostic differences on the basis of primary tumor site in neuroblastoma: a report from the international neuroblastoma risk group project."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Among 8,369 children, 47% had adrenal tumors. ... Adrenal tumors were more likely than nonadrenal tumors (adjusted odds ratio, 2.09; 95% CI, 1.67 to 2.63; P < .001) and thoracic tumors were less likely than nonthoracic tumors (adjusted odds ratio, 0.20; 95% CI, 0.11 to 0.39; P < .001) to have MYCN amplification after controlling for age, stage, and histologic grade. ... After controlling for age, MYCN status, and stage, patients with adrenal tumors had higher risk for events (hazard ratio, 1.13 compared with nonadrenal tumors; 95% CI, 1.03 to 1.23; P = .008)"
    explanation: >-
      In the INRG database cohort of children younger than 21 years diagnosed
      with neuroblastoma or ganglioneuroblastoma in 1990-2002 with a known
      primary site, 47% of the 8,369 children had adrenal primary tumors.
      Compared with non-adrenal primaries, adrenal tumors had about twice the
      odds of MYCN amplification after adjustment for age, stage and histologic
      grade (adjusted odds ratio 2.09), and a higher risk of an event after
      adjustment for age, MYCN status and stage (hazard ratio 1.13). Because the
      cohort includes ganglioneuroblastoma, the 47% is a share of this cohort,
      not a frequency among neuroblastoma alone.
stages:
- name: INRGSS Stage L1
  description: >-
    Locoregional tumor with none of the 20 image-defined risk factors (IDRFs).
    The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group Staging System (INRGSS) stages
    patients before any treatment, from clinical criteria and IDRFs, because the
    International Neuroblastoma Staging System (INSS) is a postsurgical staging
    system.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:19047290
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) staging system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Because the International Neuroblastoma Staging System (INSS) is a postsurgical staging system, a new clinical staging system was required for the INRG pretreatment risk classification system. ... To stage patients before any treatment, the INRG Task Force, consisting of neuroblastoma experts from Australia/New Zealand, China, Europe, Japan, and North America, developed a new INRG staging system (INRGSS) based on clinical criteria and image-defined risk factors (IDRFs). ... In the INGRSS, locoregional tumors are staged L1 or L2 based on the absence or presence of one or more of 20 IDRFs, respectively."
    explanation: >-
      The INRG Task Force report states that a new clinical staging system was
      required for the INRG pretreatment risk classification because the INSS is
      a postsurgical staging system. To stage patients before any treatment, the
      Task Force based the INRGSS on clinical criteria and image-defined risk
      factors (IDRFs), and it stages locoregional tumors L1 or L2 by the absence
      or presence of one or more of 20 IDRFs. These sentences give the Task
      Force's consensus definition and rationale, not patient data; INGRSS is
      the source's own misspelling, kept verbatim.
- name: INRGSS Stage L2
  description: >-
    Locoregional tumor with one or more of the 20 IDRFs. In the INRG Task
    Force's analysis of European patients with locoregional disease, 5-year
    event-free survival was lower for L2 than for L1 tumors (78% versus 90%).
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:19047290
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) staging system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "In the INGRSS, locoregional tumors are staged L1 or L2 based on the absence or presence of one or more of 20 IDRFs, respectively."
    explanation: >-
      The INRG Task Force report stages locoregional tumors L1 or L2 by the
      absence or presence of one or more of 20 image-defined risk factors, so a
      locoregional tumor with at least one of them is stage L2. This is the Task
      Force's consensus staging rule rather than a patient observation; INGRSS
      is the source's own misspelling of INRGSS.
  - reference: PMID:19047290
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) staging system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Patients with INRGSS stage L2 disease had significantly lower 5-year event-free survival than those with INRGSS stage L1 disease (78% +/- 4% v 90% +/- 3%; P = .0010)."
    explanation: >-
      The Task Force's post hoc analysis of European (SIOPEN) patients with
      locoregional (INSS stage 1 to 3) tumors reports 5-year event-free survival
      of 78% for INRGSS L2 against 90% for L1 (P = .0010). Per the full text,
      474 of the 661 patients analysed had outcome data, 213 with L1 and 261
      with L2 disease. The comparison covers locoregional tumors only.
- name: INRGSS Stage M
  description: >-
    Distant metastatic disease, except the restricted metastatic pattern in
    children younger than 18 months that is staged MS.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:19047290
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) staging system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Metastatic tumors are defined as stage M, except for stage MS, in which metastases are confined to the skin, liver, and/or bone marrow in children younger than 18 months of age."
    explanation: >-
      The INRG Task Force report defines metastatic tumors as INRGSS stage M,
      with one exception: stage MS, in which metastases are confined to skin,
      liver and/or bone marrow in children younger than 18 months. This is the
      Task Force's consensus definition, given in the results section of the
      structured abstract.
- name: INRGSS Stage MS
  description: >-
    Metastatic disease in a child younger than 18 months (547 days) with
    metastases confined to skin, liver and/or bone marrow, bone marrow
    involvement below 10% of nucleated cells, and meta-iodobenzylguanidine
    (MIBG) scintigraphy negative in bone and bone marrow; the primary tumor may
    be L1 or L2, with no restriction on crossing or infiltrating the midline.
    INSS stage 4S is the narrower INSS counterpart, limited to infants younger
    than 12 months with an INSS stage 1 or 2 primary tumor and dissemination to
    liver, skin and/or bone marrow (under 10% involvement); the INRGSS extended
    the age limit to 18 months and admitted primaries infiltrating the midline
    (INSS stage 3). In an Italian series of 30 infants with stage IV-S disease
    treated in 1970-1981, the liver was the most frequent site of spread (87%),
    and subcutaneous nodules were recorded. In infants with stage IV-S or 4S
    disease the pattern is associated with spontaneous regression and good
    survival. In two infant cohorts, one limited to symptomatic or biologically
    unfavorable cases, most deaths occurred in infants younger than 2 months at
    diagnosis, most often from complications of hepatomegaly or extensive
    abdominal involvement. In the selected cohort, enrolled on the COG trial
    ANBL0531, no further deaths from hepatomegaly occurred after the protocol
    was amended to require immediate chemotherapy for infants younger than 2
    months with evolving hepatomegaly. In a Children's Oncology Group cohort
    staged by the INRGSS, stage MS outcome was excellent except for
    MYCN-amplified tumors, which have a poor outcome. Whether toddlers aged 12
    to 18 months with a 4S pattern of metastasis share the favorable outcome of
    infants is contested. In the INRG database, toddlers grouped by metastatic
    sites alone, without the marrow limit of stage MS, had worse event-free
    survival than infants with the 4S pattern and outcomes similar to stage 4
    disease at the same age, and the authors concluded that tumor biology
    matters more than age or metastatic pattern. Registry data from two Japanese
    pediatric societies showed an excellent prognosis for stage 4s disease at 12
    to 17 months.
  notes: >-
    INSS stage 4S is recorded within this stage, not as a has_subtypes row,
    because the cancer granularity ladder (design decisions §3a) records stage
    under stages. The 4S category descends from the IV-S category of the 1971
    Evans staging system, recognizing patients with metastatic disease limited
    to skin, liver and bone marrow who have superior outcomes, and the 1993
    revision of the INSS added restrictions on age and bone marrow involvement
    for stage 4S. When the INRG Task Force extended the age limit to 18 months,
    it described the group aged 12 to 18 months as small, with an unclear
    outcome.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:19047290
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) staging system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Stage MS is metastatic disease in patients younger than 18 months (547 days) with metastases confined to skin, liver, and/or bone marrow. Bone marrow involvement should be limited to less than 10% of total nucleated cells on smears or biopsy. MIBG scintigraphy must be negative in bone and bone marrow. Provided there is MIBG uptake in the primary tumor, bone scans are not required. The primary tumor can be L1 or L2 and there is no restriction regarding crossing or infiltration of the midline."
    explanation: >-
      The INRG Task Force report that defines the INRGSS states each criterion
      of stage MS: age under 18 months (547 days); metastases confined to skin,
      liver and/or bone marrow; bone marrow involvement under 10% of nucleated
      cells; MIBG scintigraphy negative in bone and bone marrow; and an L1 or L2
      primary tumor with no restriction on crossing or infiltrating the midline.
      It is an expert-consensus definition; the report's own survival analysis
      covered only locoregional tumors.
  - reference: PMID:19047290
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) staging system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Fourth, whereas INSS stage 4S has an upper age limit of 12 months, the Task Force decided to extend the age group for stage MS to patients younger than 18 months. ... Unlike INSS stage 4S, stage MS includes patients with primary tumors infiltrating the midline (INSS stage 3)."
    explanation: >-
      The same report names two differences between stage MS and INSS stage 4S:
      INSS 4S has an upper age limit of 12 months while the Task Force extended
      MS to children younger than 18 months, and unlike 4S, MS includes children
      whose primary tumor infiltrates the midline (INSS stage 3). These are
      consensus decisions, not outcome data.
  - reference: PMID:30754710
    reference_title: "The Evolution of Risk Classification for Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "4S | Localized primary tumor as defined by stage 1 or 2 in patient under 12 months with dissemination limited to the liver, skin, and/or bone marrow (<10% involvement)"
    explanation: >-
      Table 1 of this review, which sets out the International Neuroblastoma
      Staging System, defines stage 4S as a localized stage 1 or 2 primary tumor
      in a patient under 12 months with dissemination limited to the liver, skin
      and/or bone marrow (under 10% involvement). The row reproduces the
      consensus INSS definition and reports no patient data; the comparison with
      stage MS rests on the Task Force sentences above.
  - reference: PMID:8336186
    reference_title: "Revisions of the international criteria for neuroblastoma diagnosis, staging, and response to treatment."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Substantial changes included a redefinition of the midline, restrictions on age and bone marrow involvement for stage 4S, and the recommendation that meta-iodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) scanning be implemented for evaluating the extent of disease."
    explanation: >-
      This is the 1993 consensus report that revised the INSS. Its abstract
      lists restrictions on age and bone marrow involvement for stage 4S among
      the substantial changes the revision made. The abstract does not give the
      numeric limits.
  - reference: PMID:30754710
    reference_title: "The Evolution of Risk Classification for Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In 1971, Evans et al. ... published the Evans Staging System based on extent of disease including a IV-S category, recognizing that there is a cohort of patients with metastatic disease limited to the skin, liver, and bone marrow, who have superior outcomes."
    explanation: >-
      This review states that the 1971 Evans staging system included a IV-S
      category, recognizing a group of patients with metastatic disease limited
      to the skin, liver and bone marrow who have superior outcomes. The
      sentence does not name INRGSS stage MS; that MS descends from this
      category, through INSS stage 4S, is an inference from the review's account
      of the staging systems. The ellipsis stands for an inline citation marker.
  - reference: PMID:10653863
    reference_title: "Favorable biology and outcome of stage IV-S neuroblastoma with supportive care or minimal therapy: a Children's Cancer Group study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Stage IV-S neuroblastoma is a metastatic disease associated with spontaneous regression and good survival, but 10% to 20% of infants die from early complications."
    explanation: >-
      The opening sentence of the purpose section of this prospective Children's
      Cancer Group study of 80 infants states that stage IV-S neuroblastoma is
      associated with spontaneous regression and good survival, but that 10% to
      20% of infants die from early complications. The authors give this as
      background from earlier series; their own cohort had 6 deaths among 80
      infants. The quote concerns infants with IV-S disease.
  - reference: PMID:6727772
    reference_title: "IV-S neuroblastoma: a cooperative study of 30 children."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The most frequent site of widespread disease was the liver (87%). Neither the size of the \"primary\" tumor, nor the number or size of subcutaneous nodules was of prognostic significance."
    explanation: >-
      In 30 Italian children with stage IV-S neuroblastoma (birth to 11 months,
      11 institutions, 1970-1981), the liver was the most frequent site of
      widespread disease (87%), and subcutaneous nodules were recorded, although
      their number and size did not predict outcome. The abstract does not call
      the nodules skin metastases or say how many children had them, so reading
      them as a presentation of skin metastasis is an inference. A small series
      from before the INSS, covering only children younger than 12 months.
  - reference: PMID:10653863
    reference_title: "Favorable biology and outcome of stage IV-S neuroblastoma with supportive care or minimal therapy: a Children's Cancer Group study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Five of six deaths were in infants younger than 2 months of age at diagnosis and were due to complications of extensive abdominal involvement with respiratory compromise or disseminated intravascular coagulation."
    explanation: >-
      In this prospective Children's Cancer Group study of 80 infants with stage
      IV-S neuroblastoma, managed with supportive care alone or, when
      symptomatic, low-dose therapy, five of the six deaths were in infants
      younger than 2 months at diagnosis and were due to complications of
      extensive abdominal involvement with respiratory compromise or
      disseminated intravascular coagulation. The cohort had biologically
      favorable disease (MYCN was not amplified in any of the 58 tumors tested),
      so this pattern says nothing about MYCN-amplified disease, and it rests on
      six deaths.
  - reference: PMID:30444686
    reference_title: "Defining Risk Factors for Chemotherapeutic Intervention in Infants With Stage 4S Neuroblastoma: A Report From Children's Oncology Group Study ANBL0531."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Eight of nine deaths were in patients younger than 2 months of age at diagnosis ... five acute deaths were a result of hepatomegaly and associated toxicities; two were a result of late relapse in patients with unfavorable biology; and two were a result of treatment complications. No deaths occurred after protocol-mandated pre-emptive treatment of infants younger than 2 months with hepatomegaly, regardless of symptoms."
    explanation: >-
      COG ANBL0531 enrolled a selected higher-risk subset of 49 infants with
      INSS stage 4S neuroblastoma: MYCN-non-amplified tumors with symptoms or
      impending organ dysfunction, or with unfavorable histology and/or a
      diploid DNA index. Eight of the nine deaths were in infants younger than 2
      months at diagnosis. Five were acute deaths from hepatomegaly and
      associated toxicities, two followed late relapse in infants with
      unfavorable tumor biology, and two followed treatment complications. The
      last sentence concerns infants enrolled after a protocol amendment; the
      next item gives the full-text figures. These results describe this
      selected cohort, not 4S as a whole, and the ellipsis stands for a
      bracketed age range.
  - reference: PMID:30444686
    reference_title: "Defining Risk Factors for Chemotherapeutic Intervention in Infants With Stage 4S Neuroblastoma: A Report From Children's Oncology Group Study ANBL0531."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "the protocol was amended to mandate immediate chemotherapy for patients with 4S disease younger than 2 months of age at diagnosis with evolving hepatomegaly. No deaths related to complications of hepatomegaly occurred in the subsequent 31 4S infants enrolled, including 18 who were younger than 2 months of age"
    explanation: >-
      After five deaths from hepatomegaly in the first 21 months of accrual,
      ANBL0531 was amended to require immediate chemotherapy for infants with 4S
      disease younger than 2 months at diagnosis with evolving hepatomegaly. No
      deaths from complications of hepatomegaly occurred among the 31 infants
      enrolled afterwards, 18 of them younger than 2 months. The full text
      limits the abstract's "no deaths" to deaths from hepatomegaly. This is a
      before-and-after comparison within one nonrandomized trial, with small
      numbers.
  - reference: PMID:34319759
    reference_title: "Revised Neuroblastoma Risk Classification System: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The outcome was excellent for our INRG MS cohort (EFS and OS: 85.8% +/- 2.5% and 92.1% +/- 1.9%) with the exception of those with MYCN-A tumors (EFS and OS: 59.9% +/- 17.0% and 64.3% +/- 15.7%), the only subgroup previously classified as HR"
    explanation: >-
      In the COG ANBL00B1 cohort (patients enrolled 2007-2017 and staged by
      INRGSS), the stage MS group as a whole had 5-year event-free and overall
      survival of 85.8% and 92.1%, which the authors call excellent. The
      exception was MS with MYCN-amplified tumors, at 59.9% and 64.3%, the only
      MS subgroup classified high risk under the earlier COG classifier. The
      MYCN-amplified estimates carry wide standard errors, so the subgroup is
      small.
  - reference: PMID:32932540
    reference_title: "Stage 4S Neuroblastoma: What Are the Outcomes? A Systematic Review of Published Studies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Twelve studies (544 patients) recorded MYCN status. Mortality in MYCN amplified tumors was 56%."
    explanation: >-
      Systematic review of 37 published stage 4S series (1,105 patients). In the
      12 studies (544 patients) that recorded MYCN status, mortality among
      patients with MYCN-amplified tumors was 56%. The abstract does not give
      the number of MYCN-amplified patients or say which staging definition each
      series used, and the pooled patients were managed in different ways.
  - reference: PMID:21969516
    reference_title: "Prognostic value of the stage 4S metastatic pattern and tumor biology in patients with metastatic neuroblastoma diagnosed between birth and 18 months of age."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "EFS was significantly better for infants younger than 12 months with 4S pattern than with stage 4 disease (P < .01) but similar for toddlers age 12 to 18 months with stage 4 versus 4S pattern. Among 717 patients with stage 4S pattern, patients age 12 to 18 months had worse EFS than those age younger than 12 months (P < .01). ... Tumor biology is more critical than age or metastatic pattern for prognosis of patients age younger than 18 months with metastatic neuroblastoma and should be considered for risk stratification. ... We divided the patients with stage 4 disease age 12 to 18 months into two groups--those with (n = 61) and without (n = 304) 4S pattern of metastasis--independent of size of primary tumor or extent of bone marrow involvement."
    explanation: >-
      Analysis of the INRG database (cooperative-group trials, 1990-2002) of 656
      INSS stage 4S infants younger than 12 months and 1,019 stage 4 patients
      younger than 18 months. Among the 717 patients with a 4S metastatic
      pattern, those aged 12 to 18 months had worse event-free survival than
      those younger than 12 months, and toddlers fared similarly whether their
      metastases followed the 4S or the stage 4 pattern. The authors conclude
      that tumor biology is more critical than age or metastatic pattern. The
      methods sentence shows that toddlers were grouped by metastatic pattern
      regardless of primary tumor size or the extent of bone marrow involvement,
      so the toddler group was not held to the marrow limit of stage MS. The
      first ellipsis skips the sentences naming individual prognostic factors.
  - reference: PMID:22305511
    reference_title: "Is the prognosis of stage 4s neuroblastoma in patients 12 months of age and older really excellent?"
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In the children 12 months of age and older, stage 4s cases are markedly different from stage 4 cases in regard to the clinical features and prognosis. The prognosis of stage 4s cases from >= 12 to <= 17months of age is excellent. The concept of stage MS appears to be appropriate."
    explanation: >-
      Conclusion of a retrospective review of 3,834 patients registered with two
      Japanese pediatric oncology and surgery societies between 1980 and 1998:
      in children 12 months and older, stage 4s cases differed markedly from
      stage 4 cases, prognosis at 12 to 17 months was excellent, and the authors
      judge the stage MS concept appropriate. The abstract does not say how many
      4s patients aged 12 to 17 months the conclusion rests on, and the cases
      were not staged with the INRGSS.
  - reference: PMID:19047290
    reference_title: "The International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) staging system: an INRG Task Force report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "The number of patients with \"stage 4S disease aged 12 to 18 months\" is small, but because the outcome in this patient cohort remains unclear, it is anticipated that the individual cooperative groups will give these patients special attention in prospective studies where careful stopping rules are included."
    explanation: >-
      In the discussion where the INRG Task Force extends the age limit of stage
      MS beyond the 12 months of INSS stage 4S, it states that the number of
      patients aged 12 to 18 months with otherwise classical 4S disease is small
      and that their outcome remains unclear, and it asks the cooperative groups
      to study them prospectively. This is the Task Force's judgement of
      evidence it did not itself produce, not a cohort result.
pathophysiology:
- name: Neural Crest Developmental Arrest
  description: >-
    Neuroblastoma arises from neural crest-derived sympathoadrenal progenitor
    cells that fail to complete differentiation. The tumor cells retain
    characteristics of immature neuroblasts with variable capacity for
    sympathetic neuronal differentiation.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41560679
    reference_title: "Coexpression of MYCN and ALK Induces Neuroblastoma-Like Tumors From Human iPS Cell-Derived Cranial Neural Crest Cells."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Neuroblastoma (NB) is a pediatric solid tumor originating from neural
      crest cells (NCCs), which are precursors of the sympathetic nervous system."
    explanation: >-
      States that neuroblastoma originates from neural crest cells, the
      precursors of the sympathetic nervous system, supporting the
      developmental origin this node describes. It is the opening background
      sentence of an iPSC-derived neural crest model study and describes the
      human disease, not an observation from that model.
  - reference: PMID:32296467
    reference_title: "Nervous system: Embryonal tumors: Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Neuroblastoma is a clinically heterogenous pediatric cancer of the
      sympathetic nervous system that originates from neural crest cells.
    explanation: Supports neural crest origin and clinical heterogeneity of
      neuroblastoma.
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: neural crest derived neuroblast
    term:
      id: CL:0002676
      label: neural crest derived neuroblast
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: cell differentiation
    modifier: DECREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0030154
      label: cell differentiation
  locations:
  - preferred_term: adrenal gland
    term:
      id: UBERON:0002369
      label: adrenal gland
  downstream:
  - target: MYCN-Driven Proliferation
    description: MYCN amplification drives aggressive proliferation
- name: MYCN-Driven Proliferation
  description: >-
    MYCN amplification results in massive overexpression of the MYCN
    transcription factor, a key contributor to aggressive neuroblastoma biology
    and poor prognosis. MYCN-amplified tumors have a distinct aggressive
    phenotype with rapid growth and early metastasis.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: MYCN
    term:
      id: hgnc:7559
      label: MYCN
  molecular_functions:
  - preferred_term: DNA-binding transcription factor activity
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0003700
      label: DNA-binding transcription factor activity
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: cell population proliferation
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0008283
      label: cell population proliferation
  downstream:
  - target: Telomerase Activation
    description: >-
      Amplified MYCN raises TERT transcription, which makes MYCN amplification a
      route to telomerase activation rather than a separate telomere maintenance
      mechanism. TERT expression was higher in MYCN-amplified tumours, and in a
      MYCN-amplified cell line TERT was the gene most strongly downregulated
      when MYCN was knocked down. Not every MYCN-amplified tumour takes this
      route: some express TERT as low as ALT tumours do, and forced MYCN
      overexpression did not induce TERT where the promoter was repressed.
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - "Increased TERT transcription driven by amplified MYCN"
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:26466568
      reference_title: "Telomerase activation by genomic rearrangements in high-risk neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "In addition, TERT expression was higher in MYCN-amplified tumours than in the remaining samples (P = 0.021, Fig. 2d)."
      explanation: >-
        Result from this study's series of patient tumours: TERT expression was
        higher in MYCN-amplified neuroblastomas than in tumours carrying neither
        MYCN amplification nor a TERT rearrangement (P = 0.021). Support for
        MYCN driving telomerase activation is indirect. The sentence reports
        that MYCN amplification and higher TERT RNA levels occur together in
        tumours, so it shows neither that MYCN causes the rise nor that
        telomerase enzyme activity increases; the paper measured that activity
        only in cell lines.
    - reference: PMID:26466568
      reference_title: "Telomerase activation by genomic rearrangements in high-risk neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Thus, genomic rearrangements at 5p15.33 abrogate silencing of gene expression in this chromosomal region, whereas amplified MYCN selectively upregulates TERT by transcriptional activation."
      explanation: >-
        The authors' conclusion from their tumour expression data:
        MYCN-amplified neuroblastomas upregulated TERT and one neighbouring
        AceView-annotated gene (bleyplaby) but not SLC6A18 or SLC6A19, which
        TERT-rearranged tumours also upregulated, and TERT was among the most
        highly upregulated genes in 92 MYCN-amplified versus 238 low-risk
        tumours. So amplified MYCN raises TERT selectively, whereas
        rearrangements lift silencing more broadly across the region.
        Limitation: the paper does not measure MYCN binding at TERT, so
        'transcriptional activation' is inferred from expression data and
        earlier work it cites, and the sentence concerns TERT expression, not
        telomerase activity.
    - reference: PMID:26466568
      reference_title: "Telomerase activation by genomic rearrangements in high-risk neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "TERT was the most strongly downregulated gene upon short-interfering-RNA-mediated MYCN knockdown in a MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma cell line"
      explanation: >-
        Transcriptome sequencing of a cultured MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma line
        (IMR-5/75) before and after MYCN knockdown made TERT the most strongly
        downregulated gene of all, so TERT expression in an amplified background
        depends on MYCN rather than the reverse. That direction is what the
        tumour expression comparisons reported elsewhere in the same study
        cannot establish on their own. The limitation is scope: a single
        cultured cell line, with TERT transcript level as the readout rather
        than enzymatic telomerase activity.
    - reference: PMID:32291317
      reference_title: "Telomere Maintenance Mechanisms Define Clinical Outcome in High-Risk Neuroblastoma."
      supports: REFUTE
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Surprisingly, some MYCN-Amp tumors had TERT expression as low as seen in ALT tumors"
      explanation: >-
        Bears against this edge holding in every MYCN-amplified tumour. In this
        high-risk cohort some MYCN-amplified tumours expressed TERT as low as
        ALT tumours do, so the edge's intermediate, increased TERT transcription
        in an amplified background, is not reached in every MYCN-amplified
        tumour. It qualifies the edge's universality rather than the route's
        existence: most MYCN-amplified tumours in the same comparison had high
        TERT expression.
    - reference: PMID:32291317
      reference_title: "Telomere Maintenance Mechanisms Define Clinical Outcome in High-Risk Neuroblastoma."
      supports: REFUTE
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "MYCN overexpression by itself is not sufficient to overcome the TERT repression in TERT non-expressing cells"
      explanation: >-
        Forced MYCN overexpression in neuroblastoma cell lines without MYCN
        amplification raised TERT expression only where the TERT promoter was
        intact and not repressed, so the authors conclude that MYCN cannot by
        itself overcome TERT repression. This bears against the edge holding in
        every tumour. Indirect for this edge: overexpression in non-amplified
        cell lines is not the amplified state the edge describes, and the
        readout is TERT expression rather than telomerase activity.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41560679
    reference_title: "Coexpression of MYCN and ALK Induces Neuroblastoma-Like Tumors From Human iPS Cell-Derived Cranial Neural Crest Cells."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "MYCN amplification is a key factor contributing to the poor prognosis of NB."
    explanation: >-
      Supports MYCN amplification as a key contributor to poor prognosis. The
      sentence is background in the abstract of an iPSC-derived neural crest
      model study, not a result of it; the patient-derived stage association
      is the Brodeur item below.
  - reference: PMID:6719137
    reference_title: "Amplification of N-myc in untreated human neuroblastomas correlates with advanced disease stage."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Furthermore, N-myc amplification is highly correlated with advanced stages of disease (P less than 0.001) and with the ability to grow in vitro as an established cell line, both of which are associated with a poor prognosis."
    explanation: >-
      Human clinical support for the aggressive-phenotype and poor-prognosis
      claim: in untreated primary tumors, MYCN amplification was absent in all
      15 stage 1-2 cases and present in 50% of stage 3-4 cases.
  - reference: PMID:29379199
    reference_title: "Enhancer invasion shapes MYCN-dependent transcriptional amplification in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "At oncogenic levels, MYCN associates with E-box binding motifs in an affinity-dependent manner, binding to strong canonical E-boxes at promoters and invading abundant weaker non-canonical E-boxes clustered at enhancers. Loss of MYCN leads to a global reduction in transcription, which is most pronounced at MYCN target genes with the greatest enhancer occupancy."
    explanation: >-
      Supports the molecular function bound on this node. ChIP-seq in
      MYCN-amplified human neuroblastoma cell lines places MYCN on E-box motifs
      at promoters and enhancers, and switching MYCN off in an engineered
      tet-off neuroblastoma line lowers transcription, most at the target genes
      with the greatest enhancer occupancy. That is sequence-specific binding in
      cis-regulatory regions that modulates target-gene transcription, the two
      parts of DNA-binding transcription factor activity. Cell-line evidence
      only; the INCREASED modifier rests on the amplification evidence on this
      node, since this quote shows the activity rather than its level.
  - reference: PMID:31365300
    reference_title: "Correlation Between MYCN Gene Status and MYCN Protein Expression in Neuroblastoma: A Pilot Study To Propose the Use of MYCN Immunohistochemistry in Limited-Resource Areas."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "A positive correlation between MYCN gene amplification and protein expression by IHC was seen in 22 (91.66%) of the 24 MYCN-amplified NB cases ... Two cases had weak protein expression but no gene amplification (MED: n = 1; 5.0%; NAD: n = 1; 2.9%). ... An excellent overall correlation between MYCN gene status by FISH and MYCN protein expression by IHC was confirmed."
    explanation: >-
      In a pilot cohort of 78 patient neuroblastomas, nuclear MYCN protein was
      detected by immunohistochemistry in 22 of the 24 MYCN-amplified tumors,
      and only two non-amplified tumors stained, weakly. MYCN protein therefore
      tracks amplification in patient tumors. That amplification is what raises
      the protein, and with it the transcription-factor activity bound on this
      node, is an inference from this association, which the diagnostic pilot
      did not test; the cohort was small and enriched for amplification, and
      staining was scored as present or absent.
- name: ALK Signaling Activation
  description: >-
    ALK (anaplastic lymphoma kinase) is activated by point mutations in
    approximately 8-10% of neuroblastomas at diagnosis, and by amplification in
    additional cases. In neuroblastoma cells, high expression of the wild-type
    receptor can also lead to its constitutive activation. ALK mutations are
    enriched in familial neuroblastoma and represent a therapeutic target for
    ALK inhibitors.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: ALK
    term:
      id: hgnc:427
      label: ALK
  molecular_functions:
  - preferred_term: transmembrane receptor protein tyrosine kinase activity
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0004714
      label: transmembrane receptor protein tyrosine kinase activity
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: MAPK cascade
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0000165
      label: MAPK cascade

- name: Telomerase Activation
  description: >-
    Telomerase-mediated telomere maintenance, one of the two telomere
    maintenance mechanisms in neuroblastoma. TERT rearrangements at 5p15.33
    juxtapose the TERT coding sequence to strong enhancer elements, with
    chromatin remodelling and DNA methylation of the affected region, and
    despite their structural diversity they all induced massive transcriptional
    upregulation of TERT. MYCN amplification raises TERT transcription, and some
    tumours have high TERT expression with neither alteration. In 457
    pretreatment neuroblastomas, TERT rearrangement was found in 46 and MYCN
    amplification in 93, and high TERT expression without either in 10 of 223
    tumours with expression data. TERT promoter mutations are rare: none was
    found in 131 primary tumours representing the whole spectrum of the disease,
    and a single-centre series found them in 17 of 603 tumours. Activated
    telomerase, defined by these routes, was associated with the poorest overall
    survival and was an independent prognostic marker in multivariable analyses.
    Enzymatic telomerase activity has been shown in neuroblastoma cell lines
    that carry a TERT rearrangement or MYCN amplification.
  biological_scale: MOLECULAR
  conforms_to: "enabling_replicative_immortality#Telomere Maintenance Reactivation"
  genes:
  - preferred_term: TERT
    term:
      id: hgnc:11730
      label: TERT
  molecular_functions:
  - preferred_term: telomerase activity
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0003720
      label: telomerase activity
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: telomere maintenance via telomerase
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:

      label: telomere maintenance via telomerase
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:26466568
    reference_title: "Telomerase activation by genomic rearrangements in high-risk neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Despite a large structural diversity of these rearrangements, they all induced massive transcriptional upregulation of TERT."
    explanation: >-
      Abstract result in patient tumours (whole-genome sequencing of 56, an
      extended series of 217, plus expression profiling): the TERT
      rearrangements were structurally diverse, yet all came with massive
      transcriptional upregulation of TERT. 'All' can only cover rearranged
      tumours with expression data, such as the 10 in the transcriptome
      comparison; 28 rearrangements were detected. 'Induced' is the authors'
      causal reading, backed by enhancer juxtaposition and TERT mRNA not
      tracking copy number, not by engineering a rearrangement. The quote
      concerns TERT mRNA; telomerase enzyme activity was measured only in cell
      lines.
  - reference: PMID:26466568
    reference_title: "Telomerase activation by genomic rearrangements in high-risk neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The 5p15.33 rearrangements juxtapose the TERT coding sequence to strong enhancer elements, resulting in massive chromatin remodelling and DNA methylation of the affected region."
    explanation: >-
      This abstract sentence summarises the paper's own results, mainly from
      patient tumour tissue: 5p15.33 rearrangements place TERT next to strong
      enhancer elements, with chromatin remodelling and DNA methylation of the
      affected region. The enhancer mapping rested on ChIP-seq of only three
      TERT-rearranged tumours, and part of the histone-mark survey used cell
      lines. The rise in CpG methylation across the TERT locus, measured in 39
      primary tumours (six rearranged), was also seen in MYCN-amplified tumours,
      so it is not specific to rearrangement.
  - reference: PMID:35100718
    reference_title: "Telomerase Is a Prognostic Marker of Poor Outcome and a Therapeutic Target in Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We detected TERT rearrangements in 46 of 457 cases (10.1%), MYCN amplification in 93 of 457 cases (20.4%), and elevated TERT expression in tumors lacking TERT or MYCN alterations in 10 of 223 cases (4.5%)."
    explanation: >-
      In a series of 457 pretreatment neuroblastomas, the study found TERT
      rearrangement in 46 and MYCN amplification in 93 by fluorescence in situ
      hybridization, and elevated TERT expression without either alteration in
      10 of 223 tumours profiled by microarray, a subset of the 273 also
      examined for ALT. The denominators differ, so the three percentages cannot
      be added together. The sentence itself does not mention telomerase: the
      authors class these alterations as activated telomerase in a later
      sentence, and the abstract reports no telomerase-activity assay on the
      tumours.
  - reference: PMID:35100718
    reference_title: "Telomerase Is a Prognostic Marker of Poor Outcome and a Therapeutic Target in Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The presence of activated telomerase (ie, TERT rearrangements, MYCN amplification, or high TERT expression without these alterations) was associated with poorest overall survival and was an independent prognostic marker in multivariable analyses."
    explanation: >-
      In an outcome analysis of pretreatment neuroblastomas, activated
      telomerase (TERT rearrangement, MYCN amplification, or high TERT
      expression without either) was associated with the poorest overall
      survival and was an independent prognostic marker in multivariable
      analyses. Activation is defined by genomic and expression markers, not
      enzyme activity, and the abstract names neither the covariates nor the
      number of tumours analysed (FISH for TERT and MYCN covered 457 tumours;
      microarray TERT expression covered 223). As MYCN amplification is a
      defining route, this does not show prognostic value beyond MYCN
      amplification.
  - reference: PMID:40638875
    reference_title: "Clinical Significance of TERT Promoter Mutations in Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "TERT-PM and TERT-RA were detected in 17 of 603 (2.8%) and 31of 168 (18.4%) tumors from individual patients, respectively."
    explanation: >-
      In a retrospective single-centre (MSK) review of sequenced neuroblastomas,
      TERT promoter mutations were found in 17 of 603 tumours profiled on the
      MSK-IMPACT targeted panel (2.8%) and TERT rearrangements in 31 of 168
      whole-genome-sequenced tumours (18.4%), so promoter mutations occur, but
      less often than rearrangements. The two rates come from different tumour
      sets and assays, because rearrangements were scored only by whole-genome
      sequencing. The sentence shows frequency, not telomerase activation:
      promoter-mutant tumours showed no statistically significant TERT mRNA
      difference from TERT-wild-type tumours, only a trend towards higher
      expression.
  - reference: PMID:26171145
    reference_title: "Absence of telomerase reverse transcriptase promoter mutations in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In 131 neuroblastoma primary tumors representing the whole spectrum of neuroblastoma, no TERT promoter mutations were detected."
    explanation: >-
      Sanger sequencing of a 474-bp TERT promoter region covering the C228T and
      C250T hotspots found no mutation in any of 131 pretreatment primary
      neuroblastomas from a German tumour bank, a cohort the authors describe as
      representing the whole spectrum of the disease; this is the description's
      131-tumour observation. Main limitation: zero of 131 cannot rule out a low
      frequency, and a later series of 603 tumours (PMID:40638875) found
      promoter mutations in 2.8%, mostly in high-risk disease, so the mutation
      is rare rather than absent.
  - reference: PMID:26171145
    reference_title: "Absence of telomerase reverse transcriptase promoter mutations in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In conclusion, the TERT promoter mutations are not a frequent mechanism of TERT overexpression in neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      Drawing chiefly on the 131 primary tumours, none with a promoter mutation,
      the authors conclude that promoter mutation is not a frequent mechanism of
      TERT overexpression in neuroblastoma, which supports the description's
      statement that TERT promoter mutations are rare. Their cell-line finding
      (C228T in 3 of 19 lines, all SK-N-SH and two of its subclones, with no
      correlation to TERT expression) is separate in-vitro evidence. Limitation:
      only a 474-bp region around the TERT start codon was sequenced; the

      regulatory elements as possible alternative mechanisms.
  - reference: PMID:26466568
    reference_title: "Telomerase activation by genomic rearrangements in high-risk neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Supporting a functional role of TERT, neuroblastoma cell lines bearing rearrangements or amplified MYCN exhibited both upregulated TERT expression and enzymatic telomerase activity."
    explanation: >-
      In this primary research paper, neuroblastoma cell lines with a TERT
      rearrangement or MYCN amplification showed both raised TERT expression and
      enzymatic telomerase activity; the Methods state that activity in cell
      lines was measured with a PCR-based telomeric repeat amplification

      alone. Limitation: activity was assayed only in cultured cell lines; the
      paper's tumour data report TERT expression and telomere content, not
      enzyme activity.
  downstream:
  - target: Unlimited Replicative Potential
    description: >-
      Telomerase keeps telomeres from eroding, so tumour cells can go on
      dividing. High-risk neuroblastoma cell lines with neither telomerase
      activity nor ALT showed continuous telomere shortening, and most lost
      viability in culture.
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:32291317
      reference_title: "Telomere Maintenance Mechanisms Define Clinical Outcome in High-Risk Neuroblastoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "high-risk neuroblastoma cell lines that were non-ALT, low TERT expressing, and lacked telomerase activity showed continuous shortening of telomeres with growth in vitro and 2 of 3 TERT-L/non-ALT cell lines spontaneously lost viability after multiple passages in culture"
      explanation: >-
        Three patient-derived high-risk neuroblastoma cell lines that lacked ALT
        and were negative for telomerase activity, not merely low in TERT mRNA,
        shortened their telomeres continuously with passage in culture, and 2 of
        3 spontaneously lost viability. Losing both telomere maintenance
        mechanisms therefore costs replicative capacity, which supports this
        edge by its converse. Viability held up in the third line, which had
        very high telomere content, so the finding establishes that a
        maintenance mechanism is required, not that telomerase alone suffices.
- name: Reduced ATRX/DAXX Complex Abundance
  description: >-
    Reduced abundance of the ATRX/DAXX chromatin remodelling complex, a
    recurrent molecular feature of alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) in
    neuroblastoma. ATRX encodes an ATP-dependent helicase of the SWI/SNF family
    of chromatin remodellers and, with DAXX, deposits the histone variant H3.3
    at telomeric regions. ALT-positive neuroblastomas show reduced ATRX/DAXX
    complex abundance, due either to ATRX mutation (55% of them in one cohort)
    or to low protein expression, while mutations in the complex members DAXX
    and H3F3A were extremely rare. In a pooled analysis of published
    ATRX-altered neuroblastomas, 68% of ATRX aberrations were multi-exon
    deletions, and 75% of these were predicted to be in-frame. ATRX mutation is
    strongly age-dependent: in 104 patients with metastatic disease, sampled to
    represent each age group, it was found in tumours from 14 of 32 adolescents
    and young adults, 9 of 54 children and none of 18 infants, although infant
    cases are reported. In the pooled analysis, each of the three types of ATRX
    aberration was more frequent in patients diagnosed at an older age, yet
    about 40% of the ATRX-aberrant patients were five years or younger at
    diagnosis.

ATRX forms a chromatin remodeling complex with DAXX, which performs the replication-independent deposition of the histone variant H3.3 at pericentromeric and telomeric regions."

  - reference: PMID:35384159
    reference_title: "Mutational spectrum of ATRX aberrations in neuroblastoma and associated patient and tumor characteristics."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We subdivide the ATRX aberrations into nonsense, missense, and multiexon deletions (MEDs) and show that 68% of them are MEDs. Of these MEDs, 75% are predicted to be in-frame."
    explanation: >-
      This meta-analysis pooled 127 neuroblastoma patients and three cell lines
      with ATRX aberrations from 20 published papers; all but two tumours were
      stage 4. Of the aberrations, 68% were multi-exon deletions, and 75% of the
      deletions analysed in detail (59 of 79) were shown or predicted to be
      in-frame, the figures the description gives. In-frame status is mostly
      predicted, the paper measures neither ATRX protein nor ATRX/DAXX complex
      levels, and a possible gain-of-function effect of the in-frame deletions,
      raised by the authors, still needs experimental confirmation.
  - reference: PMID:33627664
    reference_title: "Alternative lengthening of telomeres in childhood neuroblastoma from genome to proteome."

    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Mutations in the ATRX complex members DAXX and H3F3A were extremely rare"
    explanation: >-
      In whole-genome sequencing of an ALT-enriched discovery cohort of 165
      patient tumours, 60 of them ALT-positive, mutations in the ATRX complex
      members DAXX and H3F3A were extremely rare: one ATRX-wild-type tumour had
      a large inversion affecting DAXX, and another had an A92S H3F3A mutation

  - reference: PMID:22416102
    reference_title: "Association of age at diagnosis and genetic mutations in patients with neuroblastoma."

    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In both cohorts (N = 104), mutations in the ATRX gene were identified in 44% (95% CI, 28%-62%) of tumors from patients in the adolescent and young adult group (14 of 32), in 17% (95% CI, 9%-29%) of tumors from children (9 of 54), and in 0% (95% CI, 0%-17%) of tumors from infants (0 of 18)."
    explanation: >-
      Retrospective tumour sequencing in 104 patients with metastatic
      neuroblastoma (whole-genome sequencing in 40, PCR/Sanger in 64) found ATRX
      mutations in tumours from 14 of 32 adolescents and young adults (12 years
      or older), 9 of 54 children (18 months to under 12 years) and 0 of 18

  - reference: PMID:35384159
    reference_title: "Mutational spectrum of ATRX aberrations in neuroblastoma and associated patient and tumor characteristics."

    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We also confirm that all three ATRX mutation types are more often identified in patients diagnosed at an older age, but still approximately 40% of the patients are aged 5 years or younger at diagnosis."
    explanation: >-
      This pooled analysis of ATRX-aberrant neuroblastomas from 20 published
      papers (127 patients, all but two stage 4) compared age at diagnosis with

      missense and multi-exon-deletion cases were each diagnosed at an older

  - reference: PMID:27793328
