- name: Mitosis-Karyorrhexis Index
  finding_term:
    preferred_term: mitosis-karyorrhexis index (MKI)
  context: Primary or metastatic tumor tissue submitted before chemotherapy or irradiation, excluding bone-marrow metastases
  description: >-
    An INPC morphologic indicator for tumors in the neuroblastoma category:
    the number of mitotic and karyorrhectic cells per 5,000 neuroblastoma
    cells, classed as low (under 100), intermediate (100 to 200) or high (over
    200). At the Children's Oncology Group Neuroblastoma Pathology Reference
    Laboratory it is determined on primary or metastatic tumor samples
    submitted before chemotherapy or irradiation, excluding bone-marrow
    metastases. The prognostic meaning of low and intermediate MKI depends on
    age at diagnosis: among 4,282 neuroblastomas reviewed at that laboratory
    between August 2001 and March 2012, the INPC age cut-offs of 60 months for
    low MKI and 18 months for intermediate MKI were independently prognostic
    in multivariable analysis, whereas a 4-month cut-off within high MKI was
    not significant after adjustment, consistent with the INPC applying no
    age cut-off to high MKI. In a Children's Cancer Group series reported in
    2001, MYCN-amplified neuroblastomas lacked neuroblastic differentiation
    regardless of patient age and were generally linked to increased mitotic
    and karyorrhectic activity, with higher MKI classes in younger patients.
  notes: >-
    Left unbound. NCIT:C106317 Mitosis-Karyorrhexis Index and its classes
    NCIT:C118955, NCIT:C118957 and NCIT:C118958 sit under Proliferative Index
    (NCIT:C28042), a Property or Attribute concept outside the
    HistopathologyFindingTerm enum, and NCIT:C163732 Increased Mitotic
    Activity covers mitotic activity only. The class boundaries follow the
    methods of PMID:25207821 and the review PMID:35053227 (high means over
    200 per 5,000 cells, as in the NCIT:C118958 definition); the introduction
    of PMID:25207821 and the review PMID:41612478 write the high class as 200
    or more, so a count of exactly 200 is classed inconsistently between
    sources.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25207821
    reference_title: "Age-dependent prognostic effect by Mitosis-Karyorrhexis Index in neuroblastoma: a report from the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The denominator (the number of background neuroblastoma cells) of each field selected for counting the mitotic and karyorrhectic cells was determined by estimation. ... One of 3 MKI classes, i.e., L-MKI (<100/5000 cells), I-MKI (100-200/5000 cells), or H-MKI (>200/ 5000 cells), was assigned to the individual neuroblastoma tumors after the number of mitotic and karyorrhectic cells per 5000 denominator cells was calculated ... Both primary and metastatic tumor samples were eligible for MKI determination, as long as they were submitted before chemotherapy/irradiation therapy was started. One exception was metastatic neuroblastoma in the bone marrow, where mitotic and karyorrhectic activities were not necessarily the same as those in the primary tumor and were not useful for prognostic evaluation"
    explanation: >-
      Methods of a Children's Oncology Group cohort study of 4,282
      neuroblastomas reviewed at the COG Neuroblastoma Pathology Reference
      Laboratory. Each tumor was assigned one of the three INPC MKI classes,
      citing the 1999 INPC criteria: the number of mitotic and karyorrhectic
      cells per 5,000 denominator cells, low under 100, intermediate 100-200
      and high over 200, where the denominator, the number of neuroblastoma
      cells in each counted field, was estimated rather than counted. Primary
      or metastatic samples were eligible only if submitted before
      chemotherapy or irradiation began; metastatic neuroblastoma in the bone
      marrow was the stated exception, because its mitotic and karyorrhectic
      activity was not necessarily the same as the primary tumor's and was not
      useful for prognostic evaluation, which the authors base on unpublished
      data. These sentences state the laboratory's practice rather than a rule
      quoted from the INPC.
  - reference: PMID:35053227
    reference_title: "Genetic and Histopathological Heterogeneity of Neuroblastoma and Precision Therapeutic Approaches for Extremely Unfavorable Histology Subgroups."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The INPC also includes three classes of mitosis-karyorrhexis index (MKI)-low (<100/5000 cells), intermediate (100-200/5000 cells) and high (>200/5000 cells)-as another morphologic indicator for tumors in the Neuroblastoma category."
    explanation: >-
      A 2022 review by Shimada and Ikegaki restates the three INPC MKI classes
      for tumors in the neuroblastoma category: low under 100, intermediate
      100-200 and high over 200 per 5,000 cells. It supports the class
      boundaries only; it does not say how the count is made or which samples
      may be scored, and it restates the INPC rather than reporting new data.
  - reference: PMID:25207821
    reference_title: "Age-dependent prognostic effect by Mitosis-Karyorrhexis Index in neuroblastoma: a report from the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "A total of 4,282 neuroblastomas reviewed at the Children's Oncology Group Neuroblastoma Pathology Reference Laboratory (8/1/2001-3/31/2012) included 2,365 low-MKI (L-MKI), 1,068 intermediate-MKI (I-MKI), and 849 high-MKI (H-MKI) tumors. ... Multivariate analyses revealed that cut-offs of 60 and 18 months for L-MKI and I-MKI tumors, respectively, were independently prognostic. However, the cut-off of 4 months for H-MKI tumors did not reach statistical significance in the presence of other factors. The age cut-offs for MKI classes (60 months for L-MKI, 18 months for I-MKI, no cut-off for H-MKI) in the current INPC are reasonable and effective for distinguishing prognostic groups with increased risk of event/death for older patients."
    explanation: >-
      Primary result of a Children's Oncology Group cohort of 4,282 centrally
      reviewed neuroblastomas (2,365 with low, 1,068 with intermediate and 849
      with high MKI). In backward-selected Cox models, fitted on the cases with
      complete prognostic data (2,273 with low, 1,009 with intermediate and
      809 with high MKI) and offering INSS stage, MYCN status, DNA index and
      grade as covariates, the INPC age cut-offs of 60 months for low MKI and
      18 months for intermediate MKI stayed independently prognostic, while a
      4-month cut-off within high MKI did not. The authors conclude that the
      INPC age scheme, with no age cut-off for high MKI, is reasonable and
      effective. Before adjustment, a cut-off of 3-4 months did separate
      high-MKI outcomes, so the absence of a cut-off reflects no independent
      age effect, not identical outcomes at every age.
  - reference: PMID:11745206
    reference_title: "Histopathology (International Neuroblastoma Pathology Classification) and MYCN status in patients with peripheral neuroblastic tumors: a report from the Children's Cancer Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Histologically, MYCN-amplified tumors lacked neuroblastic differentiation regardless of the age of patients. MYCN amplification also was linked generally to increased mitotic and karyorrhectic activities. However, MKI classes in patients with MYCN-amplified tumors varied significantly, depending on the age at diagnosis, and younger patients had higher MKI classes."
    explanation: >-
      In a Children's Cancer Group series of 628 peripheral neuroblastic tumors
      evaluated by the INPC and tested for MYCN status, the comparison of
      morphology with MYCN status used the 535 tumors in the neuroblastoma
      category. MYCN-amplified tumors lacked neuroblastic differentiation
      regardless of patient age, MYCN amplification was generally linked to
      increased mitotic and karyorrhectic activity, and among MYCN-amplified
      tumors the MKI class varied with age at diagnosis, younger patients
      having higher classes. The abstract reports these as associations in
      one series and gives no per-class counts or age cut-offs.
- name: INPC Favorable Histology
  finding_term:
    preferred_term: INPC favorable histology
  context: Primary or metastatic tumor tissue obtained before chemotherapy or irradiation
  description: >-
    The INPC favorable-histology group as defined for the neuroblastoma
    category: poorly differentiated or differentiating tumors with a low or
    intermediate mitosis-karyorrhexis index in patients younger than 18
    months, and differentiating tumors with a low index in patients aged 18
    months to 5 years. Among 630 neuroblastoma-category tumors in a
    Children's Cancer Group pathology review reported in 2001, this subgroup
    had 90.4% 5-year event-free survival. Under the INPC the grouping is to be
    determined only from primary or metastatic tumor tissue obtained before
    chemotherapy or irradiation, and once assigned it is not to be changed
    during the clinical course, because therapy-associated histologic changes
    may not have proven prognostic significance. The Children's Oncology
    Group and International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) classifications
    use INPC histology differently: the Children's Oncology Group stratifies
    treatment using age together with histology classified by the age-linked
    INPC criteria, which by definition duplicates the prognostic contribution
    of age, whereas the INRG classification incorporates individual
    histologic features underlying INPC. A 2020 analysis of the INRG Data
    Commons recommended replacing INPC with those individual features in the
    Children's Oncology Group classification as well; that was a proposal,
    and when it was published the Children's Oncology Group classification
    still combined INPC histology with age.
  notes: >-
    Left unbound. NCIT:C85414 Favorable Shimada Classification sits under
    NCIT:C85413 Shimada Classification System, outside the
    HistopathologyFindingTerm enum, and its definition is written in the
    original Shimada terms (differentiated or undifferentiated neuroblasts,
    stroma-rich tumors without a nodular pattern) rather than INPC's three
    named differentiation grades. NCIT:C177565 International Neuroblastoma
    Pathology Classification Histologic Group is a qualifier under
    NCIT:C28076 Disease Grade Qualifier, also outside the enum. No frequency
    is given because the share of favorable histology depends on the age and
    risk mix of the cohort.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:11745303
    reference_title: "International neuroblastoma pathology classification for prognostic evaluation of patients with peripheral neuroblastic tumors: a report from the Children's Cancer Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "There were 630 NB tumors, 30 GNBi tumors, 10 GN tumors, and 76 GNBn tumors. In the NB category, prognostic effects of the indicators ... were affected significantly by the age of the patients. The age-linked evaluation of the indicators according to the International Classification successfully distinguished two prognostic subgroups: the favorable histology (FH) subgroup (PD/D and L/I-MKI tumors in patients age < 1.5 years, D and L-MKI tumors in patients ages 1.5-5.0 years; 90.4% 5-year event free survival [EFS])"
    explanation: >-
      This 2001 Children's Cancer Group report evaluated pathology slides from
      746 peripheral neuroblastic tumors in the CCG-3881 and CCG-3891 studies
      according to the INPC (the abstract's methods name the studies, outside
      the quote); 630 were in the neuroblastoma category. In that category the
      prognostic effects of differentiation grade and MKI depended on age, and
      the age-linked evaluation distinguished a favorable histology subgroup
      with 90.4% 5-year event-free survival: poorly differentiated or
      differentiating tumors with low or intermediate MKI before 1.5 years (18
      months), and differentiating tumors with low MKI at 1.5-5.0 years. The
      criteria are the classification's own, applied here rather than derived.
      The figure belongs to the neuroblastoma category, distinct from the
      90.8% the same paper reports for the favorable group across all
      categories, and it reflects the treatment era of these studies rather
      than current outcomes.
  - reference: PMID:41612478
    reference_title: "Pathology of peripheral neuroblastic tumors."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "The distinction of FH group or UH group according to the INPC, as summarized in Table 1, should only be determined based on the pathology review of primary or metastatic tumors obtained before starting chemotherapy/irradiation therapy. Once FH or UH group classification is assigned, it should not be changed throughout the clinical course of individual cases, since therapy-associated histology changes including neuroblastic cytodifferentiation and even Schwannian stromal development, if present, may not have proven prognostic significance"
    explanation: >-
      A 2026 narrative review restates the INPC rule, citing among others the
      1999 INPC paper: the favorable or unfavorable histology group should be
      determined only from pathology review of primary or metastatic tumors
      obtained before chemotherapy or irradiation starts, and once assigned it
      should not be changed during the clinical course, because
      therapy-associated changes such as neuroblastic cytodifferentiation and
      Schwannian stromal development may not have proven prognostic
      significance. The passage states a classification rule and reports no
      patient data, so it is graded OTHER.
  - reference: PMID:32315273
    reference_title: "Age, Diagnostic Category, Tumor Grade, and Mitosis-Karyorrhexis Index Are Independently Prognostic in Neuroblastoma: An INRG Project."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The Children's Oncology Group (COG) stratifies the treatment of patients with neuroblastoma on the basis of a combination of biomarkers that include age and tumor histology classified by age-linked International Neuroblastoma Pathology Classification (INPC) criteria. By definition, this leads to a duplication of the prognostic contribution of age. The individual histologic features underlying the INPC have prognostic strength and are incorporated in the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group classification schema."
    explanation: >-
      The authors state that the Children's Oncology Group stratifies
      treatment on a combination of biomarkers that includes age and tumor
      histology classified by the age-linked INPC criteria, which by
      definition duplicates the prognostic contribution of age, while the INRG
      classification schema incorporates individual histologic features
      underlying INPC. This is the contrast in how the two risk
      classifications use INPC histology. These are framing sentences from the
      purpose statement of an INRG Data Commons cohort study, restated in its
      introduction with citations to earlier work, not the study's own
      result; they name the INPC criteria rather than the favorable and
      unfavorable histology groups.
  - reference: PMID:32315273
    reference_title: "Age, Diagnostic Category, Tumor Grade, and Mitosis-Karyorrhexis Index Are Independently Prognostic in Neuroblastoma: An INRG Project."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Event-free survival of patients diagnosed between 1990 and 2002 (cohort 1; n = 10,104) and between 2003 and 2016 (cohort 2; n = 8,761) was analyzed. ... Replacing INPC with individual histologic features in the COG risk classification will eliminate confounding, facilitate international harmonization of risk classification, and provide a schema for more precise prognostication and refined therapeutic approaches."
    explanation: >-
      A survival-tree analysis of two INRG Data Commons cohorts (10,104
      patients diagnosed 1990-2002 and 8,761 diagnosed 2003-2016) concludes
      that replacing INPC with individual histologic features in the COG risk
      classification will eliminate confounding and aid international
      harmonization of risk classification. The confounding is the double
      counting of age, since INPC is itself age-linked; the same paper found
      INPC highly prognostic of event-free survival in univariate analyses.
      This is the authors' recommendation as published in 2020; the quote
      does not say whether the Children's Oncology Group adopted it.
- name: INPC Unfavorable Histology
  finding_term:
    preferred_term: INPC unfavorable histology
  context: Primary or metastatic tumor tissue obtained before chemotherapy or irradiation
  description: >-
    The INPC unfavorable-histology group as defined for the neuroblastoma
    category: undifferentiated tumors and tumors with a high
    mitosis-karyorrhexis index at any age; poorly differentiated tumors, and
    tumors with an intermediate index, in patients aged 18 months to 5 years;
    and any neuroblastoma-category tumor in patients aged 5 years or older.
    The pre-treatment tissue rule and the differing use of the grouping by the
    Children's Oncology Group and INRG risk classifications apply as for
    favorable histology (see INPC Favorable Histology). In a Children's Cancer
    Group pathology review of tumors from the CCG-3881 and CCG-3891 studies,
    reported in 2001, this subgroup had 26.9% event-free survival. That figure
    belongs to its cohort and era: a 2022 review gives 5-year event-free
    survival of 54.6% for unfavorable and 88.1% for favorable histology
    (5-year overall survival 65.6% and 96.4%), citing the cohort analyzed for
    the 2021 revised Children's Oncology Group risk classification. In
    high-risk disease, histology after induction chemotherapy differs from the
    diagnostic histology, but the difference has not been shown to be
    prognostic: in paired diagnostic and post-induction resection samples from
    94 high-risk patients on Children's Oncology Group trials (2001-2013),
    tumors resected after induction chemotherapy had shifted toward a more
    differentiated, less mitotically active histology, and neither histologic
    features at resection nor their change from diagnosis was significantly
    associated with progression-free or overall survival.
  notes: >-
    Left unbound. NCIT:C85415 Unfavorable Shimada Classification sits under
    NCIT:C85413 Shimada Classification System, outside the
    HistopathologyFindingTerm enum, and its definition is written in the
    original Shimada terms rather than INPC's three named differentiation
    grades. No frequency is given because the share of unfavorable histology
    depends on the age and risk mix of the cohort.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:11745303
    reference_title: "International neuroblastoma pathology classification for prognostic evaluation of patients with peripheral neuroblastic tumors: a report from the Children's Cancer Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Pathology slides from 746 NTs (the Children's Cancer Group ... -3881 and CCG-3891 studies) were evaluated according to the International Classification. ... In the NB category, prognostic effects of the indicators ... were affected significantly by the age of the patients. The age-linked evaluation of the indicators according to the International Classification successfully distinguished two prognostic subgroups: ... the unfavorable histology (UH) subgroup (U and/or H-MKI tumors in patients of any age, PD and/or I-MKI tumors in patients ages 1.5-5.0 years, any grade of differentiation, and any MKI class in patients age > or = 5 years; 26.9% EFS) (P < 0.0001)."
    explanation: >-
      Shimada et al. evaluated pathology slides from 746 neuroblastic tumors
      from the Children's Cancer Group CCG-3881 and CCG-3891 studies according
      to the INPC; the ellipsis inside the study names replaces the abstract's
      bracketed abbreviation of the group's name. Within the neuroblastoma
      category (630 of the 746 tumors), the age-linked evaluation
      distinguished an unfavorable histology subgroup: undifferentiated (U) or
      high-MKI tumors at any age, poorly differentiated (PD) or
      intermediate-MKI tumors at 1.5-5.0 years (18 months to 5 years), and
      tumors of any grade and MKI class at 5 years or older. That subgroup had
      26.9% event-free survival; the abstract gives no time point for this
      figure. The criteria are the classification's own, applied here rather
      than derived. The figure is historical (published 2001) and covers only
      the neuroblastoma-category subgroup; the unfavorable group across
      categories had 31.2%.
  - reference: PMID:35053227
    reference_title: "Genetic and Histopathological Heterogeneity of Neuroblastoma and Precision Therapeutic Approaches for Extremely Unfavorable Histology Subgroups."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "As mentioned above, the INPC offers the prognostic distinction between the FH group (5-year EFS+/-SE of 88.1+/-0.9; 5-year OS+/-SE of 96.4+/- 0.5) and UH group (5-year EFS+/-SE of 54.6+/-1.3; 5-year OS+/-SE of 65.6+/-1.3)"
    explanation: >-
      The review reports 5-year event-free survival of 88.1% (SE 0.9) for the
      INPC favorable histology group and 54.6% (SE 1.3) for the unfavorable
      group, with 5-year overall survival of 96.4% and 65.6%. The quote states
      the figures but not their cohort; the review attributes them to the
      2021 revised Children's Oncology Group risk-classification report, so
      the cohort named in the description rests on the review's citation
      rather than on the quote, which makes the support indirect. The review
      restates that result rather than reporting new data.
  - reference: PMID:41294259
    reference_title: "Histologic Response to Induction Chemotherapy in High-Risk Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Tumor histology from paired samples at diagnosis and resection was evaluated from 94 patients with high-risk neuroblastoma enrolled in Children's Oncology Group (COG) trials from 2001 to 2013. ... Our findings suggest that primary neuroblastoma tumors undergo a significant morphologic shift following induction chemotherapy to a differentiated, less mitotically active phenotype. However, the alterations are not prognostic of patient outcome either at resection alone, or when the change from diagnosis to resection is considered."
    explanation: >-
      Primary result of a retrospective study of paired diagnostic and
      post-induction resection tissue from 94 patients with high-risk
      neuroblastoma enrolled in Children's Oncology Group trials from 2001 to
      2013. The abstract reports a significant shift after induction
      chemotherapy toward a differentiated, less mitotically active
      phenotype, and no prognostic value for histology at resection or for
      the change from diagnosis. Here, not prognostic means no statistically
      significant association with progression-free or overall survival in a
      cohort of this size: the shift from intermediate or high MKI at
      diagnosis to low MKI at resection had hazard ratios of 2.1 for
      progression-free survival (p = 0.0908) and 2.3 for overall survival
      (p = 0.0773). The study scored individual INPC features rather than
      reassigning favorable or unfavorable histology at resection, and most
      tumors already had unfavorable features at diagnosis. It does not state
      or test the INPC rule that the grouping is assigned on pre-treatment
      tissue.

phenotypes:
- category: Abdominal
  name: Abdominal Mass
  frequency: OCCASIONAL
  diagnostic: true
  description: >-
    An abdominal mass is among the most frequent presenting signs, alongside
    fever, abdominal pain and bone pain. Most primary tumors arise in the
    abdomen or pelvis, half of these in the adrenal medulla.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Abdominal mass
    term:
      id: HP:0031500
      label: Abdominal mass
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:10985139
    reference_title: "Neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Seventy-five percent of neuroblastomas originate within the abdomen or pelvis, and half of these occur within the adrenal medulla"
    explanation: >-
      Review summary of primary-tumor site: seventy-five percent of
      neuroblastomas originate within the abdomen or pelvis, and half of these
      within the adrenal medulla. It supports the description's statement that
      most primary tumors arise in the abdomen or pelvis, half of them in the
      adrenal medulla. It bears on the phenotype only by inference, since a
      primary tumor there can present as an abdominal mass. It gives where
      tumors arise, not how often an abdominal mass is the presenting sign, so
      it does not set the frequency band.
  - reference: PMID:29995142
    reference_title: "CLINICAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL CHARACTERISTICS AND SURVIVAL OUTCOMES OF CHILDREN WITH NEUROBLASTOMA: 21 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE AT THE INSTITUTO DE ONCOLOGIA PEDIÁTRICA, IN SÃO PAULO, BRAZIL."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The most frequent manifestations were: fever (25%), abdominal pain (22%), abdominal mass (19%), and bone pain (19%)."
    explanation: >-
      Retrospective single-center series of patients with neuroblastoma of all
      INSS stages admitted over two decades to the Instituto de Oncologia
      Pediátrica in São Paulo. An abdominal mass was one of the four most
      frequent presenting manifestations, at 19% in the abstract, behind fever
      (25%) and abdominal pain (22%) and level with bone pain (19%). That figure
      falls in the occasional band, and a mass was not the most common
      presentation in this series. The results text and the signs-and-symptoms
      table give slightly higher figures for the same sign, all within the same
      band; the table records abdominal distension as a separate sign. The
      figure counts a mass recorded among the signs and symptoms at
      presentation. It is not the share of patients whose primary tumor lay in
      the abdomen, which the same abstract names as the most common tumor site,
      so a band taken from it rests on how often a mass was recorded as a
      presenting sign and may understate how many patients had an abdominal
      mass. Limitations: one specialist center, mostly advanced disease, a
      longer interval from symptom onset to diagnosis than in the United States
      and Edinburgh series the authors cite, and patients ranging from newborns
      to young adults.
  - reference: PMID:42680795
    reference_title: "Musculoskeletal symptoms and misdiagnoses among children with neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Table 2. Clinical presentation of paediatric patients with and without MS misdiagnoses prior to the diagnosis of neuroblastoma. ... Palpable mass 12% (2/17) 29% (36/126)"
    explanation: >-
      In this nationwide, population-based Danish cohort of children with
      neuroblastoma, the clinical presentation table records a palpable mass in
      2 of the 17 children who received a musculoskeletal misdiagnosis and in 36
      of the 126 who did not, so in 38 of 143 children overall (38/143 = 26.6%),
      within the OCCASIONAL band. The row does not give the site of the mass, so
      for an abdominal mass the figure is an upper bound and supports the band
      indirectly.
  phenotype_contexts:
  - population: "Children aged 0-15 years diagnosed 2010-2020 at Ugandan centers (75 patients; stage 4 in 70.7%)"
    frequency: "65.3%"
    notes: >-
      The Ugandan review records abdominal swelling and abdominal mass as one
      feature at diagnosis (65.3%), so the figure may include children with
      abdominal swelling but no discrete mass. HPO lists abdominal swelling as
      an exact synonym of its separate abdominal distention term, and the São
      Paulo series counts abdominal distension apart from a mass, so the two
      figures are not directly comparable. The review was not restricted by
      stage, but the cohort was diagnosed at a median age of 48 months and
      mostly with stage 4 disease (70.7%), so its figure reflects mostly
      advanced disease at diagnosis in this setting and does not set the
      phenotype's overall frequency.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:36562399
      reference_title: "A retrospective evaluation of the presentation, prognostic factors and outcomes of neuroblastoma in Ugandan children."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "The study was a multicenter retrospective chart review of children aged between 0 to 15 years diagnosed with NB from 2010 to 2020. ... Seventy-five patients were evaluated, with a median age at diagnosis of 48 months (IQR 26-108 months). Fever (74.7%), weight loss (74.7%), high blood pressure (70.3%) and abdominal swelling/mass (65.3%) were the most common features at diagnosis. Suprarenal tumors (52%) and stage 4 disease (70.7%) were also common."
      explanation: >-
        Multicenter retrospective chart review of seventy-five Ugandan children
        with neuroblastoma. Abdominal swelling or mass was recorded at diagnosis
        in 65.3%, after fever and weight loss (74.7% each) and high blood
        pressure (70.3%); stage 4 disease (70.7%) was also common. The source
        counts swelling and mass as one feature, and HPO files abdominal
        swelling under a separate term, abdominal distention, so the figure may
        include children with swelling but no discrete mass. The review was not
        restricted by stage, but most of the cohort had stage 4 disease at
        diagnosis, so the figure reflects mostly advanced disease at diagnosis
        in this setting.
- category: Gastrointestinal
  name: Abdominal Pain
  frequency: OCCASIONAL
  description: >-
    Abdominal pain is among the most frequent presenting symptoms, alongside
    fever, abdominal mass and bone pain.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Abdominal pain
    term:
      id: HP:0002027
      label: Abdominal pain
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29995142
    reference_title: "CLINICAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL CHARACTERISTICS AND SURVIVAL OUTCOMES OF CHILDREN WITH NEUROBLASTOMA: 21 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE AT THE INSTITUTO DE ONCOLOGIA PEDIÁTRICA, IN SÃO PAULO, BRAZIL."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The most frequent manifestations were: fever (25%), abdominal pain (22%), abdominal mass (19%), and bone pain (19%)."
    explanation: >-
      In the São Paulo series, a retrospective review of the medical records of
      patients with neuroblastoma of all INSS stages treated at one pediatric
      oncology center from 1991 to 2012, abdominal pain was recorded as a
      presenting manifestation in 22%, second only to fever among the
      individually named signs. The results text and the signs-and-symptoms
      table give the same figure, and 22% falls in the OCCASIONAL band.
      Limitations: a single specialist center rather than a population-based
      sample, a case mix weighted toward advanced disease, and ages at diagnosis
      from the newborn period into young adulthood.
- category: Gastrointestinal
  name: Abdominal Distension
  frequency: OCCASIONAL
  description: >-
    Abdominal distension is recorded as a presenting sign in its own right,
    separately from a palpable abdominal mass.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Abdominal distension
    term:
      id: HP:0003270
      label: Abdominal distention
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29995142
    reference_title: "CLINICAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL CHARACTERISTICS AND SURVIVAL OUTCOMES OF CHILDREN WITH NEUROBLASTOMA: 21 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE AT THE INSTITUTO DE ONCOLOGIA PEDIÁTRICA, IN SÃO PAULO, BRAZIL."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Distribution of the signs and symptoms in 258 patients with neuroblastoma. ... Abdominal distension | 46 (18%)"
    explanation: >-
      In the signs-and-symptoms table of the São Paulo series of 258 patients
      with neuroblastoma of all INSS stages, abdominal distension was recorded
      in 46 (46/258 = 18%), as a sign separate from abdominal mass, within the
      OCCASIONAL band. Limitations: one specialist center and a case mix
      weighted toward advanced disease.
- category: Cardiovascular
  name: Hypertension
  frequency: OCCASIONAL
  description: >-
    Hypertension at diagnosis can be asymptomatic, so reported frequencies
    differ widely between a series that measured blood pressure and counts of
    children who presented symptoms of hypertension. Its causes are
    multifactorial. It is often attributed to a renin-mediated effect when the
    tumor compresses the renal artery or renal parenchyma. A registry survey
    could not demonstrate a correlation between hypertension and compression of
    the renal vascular pedicle, but found involvement of the renal pedicle to be
    the only risk factor consistently associated with hypertension persisting
    after surgery. A neuroendocrine (catecholamine) contribution has also been
    proposed but is debated: plasma catecholamines are lower in neuroblastoma
    than in pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma, and the same survey could not
    demonstrate a correlation between hypertension and the secretion of specific
    catecholamines.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Hypertension
    term:
      id: HP:0000822
      label: Hypertension
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:17023826
    reference_title: "Hypertension in childhood cancer: a frequent complication of certain tumor sites."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Retrospective descriptive study of the case files of 31 patients followed in the Institut Curie Department of Pediatric Oncology between 1999 and 2004 and presenting severe HT at the time of diagnosis of their tumor ... The tumors presented by these children were: Wilms tumor (n=17, ie, 20% of all Wilms tumors treated during this period), neuroblastoma (n=12, ie, 10% of all neuroblastomas treated during this period) or other tumors (n=2). HT was asymptomatic in all children."
    explanation: >-
      Retrospective review of the case files of the 31 children with severe
      hypertension at the diagnosis of their tumor who were followed in the
      Institut Curie Department of Pediatric Oncology between 1999 and 2004.
      Twelve had neuroblastoma, which the authors give as 10% of all
      neuroblastomas treated there in that period; 10% falls in the OCCASIONAL
      band. The series counted only severe hypertension, so hypertension of any
      degree at diagnosis was at least this frequent at that center.
      Hypertension was asymptomatic in all 31 children, so counts restricted to
      children who presented symptoms of hypertension would miss such cases.
      Limitation: a single center.
  - reference: PMID:34612613
    reference_title: "Catecholamines in neuroblastoma: Driver of hypertension, or solely a marker of disease?"
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Hypertension is often attributed to renin-mediated effect when renal artery or parenchymal compression is present."
    explanation: >-
      Introduction of a single-center series of children with neuroblastoma and
      hypertension, restating earlier reports: hypertension in neuroblastoma is
      often attributed to a renin-mediated effect when renal artery or
      parenchymal compression is present. It supports the description's
      statement of the usual attribution; it is not a result measured in this
      series.
  - reference: PMID:36531507
    reference_title: "Low number of neurosecretory vesicles in neuroblastoma impairs massive catecholamine release and prevents hypertension."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Hypertension, a typical clinical symptom of CAT-producing tumors, has a low prevalence in NB, ranging from 2.2% to 10% in two recent reports and is mainly related to renal artery compression, which frequently resolves after tumor resection"
    explanation: >-
      Background sentence in the introduction of a study of catecholamine
      storage and release in neuroblastoma: hypertension has a low prevalence in
      neuroblastoma, from 2.2% to 10% in two recent reports, and is mainly
      related to renal artery compression, which frequently resolves after tumor
      resection. It supports the description's statements that reported
      frequencies differ widely and that renal artery compression is the usual
      attribution. The sentence summarizes earlier reports rather than adding
      data from this study.
  - reference: PMID:34612613
    reference_title: "Catecholamines in neuroblastoma: Driver of hypertension, or solely a marker of disease?"
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "All patients (n = 10) had elevated urine normetanephrine levels and eight had intra-abdominal tumors. Four patients had refractory hypertension requiring > three agents, of which three required alpha/beta blockade. ... Although multifactorial, hypertension in neuroblastoma often has a neuroendocrine component."
    explanation: >-
      Single-center retrospective series of children with neuroblastoma selected
      for at least stage II hypertension. All 10 had raised urine
      normetanephrine, and three of the four with refractory hypertension needed
      alpha/beta blockade; from this the authors conclude that hypertension in
      neuroblastoma, although multifactorial, often has a neuroendocrine
      component. It supports the description's statements that the causes are
      multifactorial and that a catecholamine contribution has been proposed.
      The conclusion is a proposal rather than a demonstrated mechanism: the
      series had no normotensive comparison group, and the paper itself notes
      that urinary catecholamine metabolites are raised in most children with
      neuroblastoma at diagnosis, so raised normetanephrine alone cannot tell a
      cause of hypertension from a marker of the tumor. The authors also state
      that they cannot say whether milder hypertension shares this component.
      Because every child was selected for hypertension, the series gives no
      frequency of hypertension in neuroblastoma.
  - reference: PMID:36531507
    reference_title: "Low number of neurosecretory vesicles in neuroblastoma impairs massive catecholamine release and prevents hypertension."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Plasma levels of metanephrines were comparable between NB and PHEO patients, while catecholamines were 3.5-fold lower in NB vs PHEO affected individuals."
    explanation: >-
      In plasma from neuroblastoma patients at diagnosis and from patients with
      pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma, metanephrines were comparable but
      catecholamines were 3.5-fold lower in neuroblastoma. Pheochromocytoma and
      paraganglioma are the tumors in which catecholamine-driven hypertension is
      typical, so this supports the description's statement that a catecholamine
      contribution in neuroblastoma is debated. The support is indirect: the
      study reports no blood pressure data, and the paper's own discussion calls
      the plasma difference slight and rests its main conclusion on far lower
      intratumoral catecholamine stores and scarce neurosecretory vesicles. The
      quoted sentence says nothing about how often hypertension occurs.
      Elsewhere the paper describes the incidence of hypertension in
      neuroblastoma as low and refers to rare patients diagnosed with
      tumor-induced hypertension, so it does not exclude a catecholamine
      contribution in individual patients.
  - reference: PMID:28711167
    reference_title: "Perioperative management of hypertensive neuroblastoma: A study from the Italian Group of Pediatric Surgical Oncologists (GICOP)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Involvement of the renal pedicle was the only risk factor constantly associated to HT persistency following surgery. A correlation between the presence of HT and the secretion of specific catecholamines and/or compression of the renal vascular pedicle could not be demonstrated."
    explanation: >-
      In the Italian registry survey of children with neuroblastoma who
      presented symptoms of hypertension, involvement of the renal pedicle was
      the only risk factor consistently associated with hypertension persisting
      after surgery, and a correlation between the presence of hypertension and
      the secretion of specific catecholamines and/or compression of the renal
      vascular pedicle could not be demonstrated. This supports the
      description's statements about the renal pedicle and the debated
      catecholamine contribution. It is a null result from a retrospective
      survey of hypertensive children, so it does not exclude a catecholamine or
      renal vascular contribution in individual patients.
  phenotype_contexts:

    frequency: "1.8%"

      (1.8%) were included in a multicenter survey. The survey counted only
      children who presented symptoms, and hypertension at diagnosis can be
      asymptomatic, so 1.8% is a lower bound and does not set the phenotype's

- category: Ophthalmologic
  name: Proptosis
  frequency: OCCASIONAL
  description: >-
    Orbital metastases cause proptosis or periorbital ecchymosis, often
    bilateral.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Proptosis
    term:
      id: HP:0000520
      label: Proptosis
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:6493702
    reference_title: "Ocular involvement in neuroblastoma: prognostic implications."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "On retrospective review of children seen at the Hospital for Sick Children, ophthalmic involvement was seen in 80 of 405 (20%). The three major eye signs of neuroblastoma, proptosis, Horner's syndrome and opsoclonus, are closely related to the site, stage of tumor, and outcome of the patient. Proptosis or periorbital ecchymosis due to orbital metastases was present in 60 of 80 children (bilaterally in 33)."
    explanation: >-
      On retrospective review of children with neuroblastoma seen at the
      Hospital for Sick Children, 80 of 405 (20%) had ophthalmic involvement,
      and in 60 of those 80, proptosis or periorbital ecchymosis due to orbital
      metastases was present, bilaterally in 33. The abstract also names
      proptosis as one of the three major eye signs of neuroblastoma. At 60 of
      405 children (60/405 = 14.8%), the combined sign falls in the OCCASIONAL
      band. The 60 can include children with periorbital ecchymosis and no
      proptosis, and the abstract gives no proptosis-only count, so 60 of 405 is
      an upper bound for proptosis from orbital metastases, and reading it as a
      proptosis frequency takes an inference step. Whether proptosis alone
      reaches the band depends on how the 60 divide between the two signs, which
      the abstract does not report. Nor does the abstract say whether these
      signs were present at diagnosis or arose later in the disease course, so
      the count should not be read as a presenting-sign frequency. The series
      covers one hospital's patients, not restricted by stage, and the abstract
      gives no study period.
  - reference: PMID:20149339
    reference_title: "Incidence, ocular manifestations, and survival in children with neuroblastoma: a population-based study."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The medical records of all pediatric (<19 years) residents of Olmsted County, Minnesota, diagnosed with neuroblastoma from January 1, 1969, through December 31, 2008, were retrospectively reviewed. ... Six of the 14 (43%; 95% CI: 18%-71%) had ocular manifestations, including orbital metastasis in 6 (100%), proptosis and ecchymosis in 4 (67%), ptosis in 2 (33%), and strabismus in 1 (17%). ... In this cohort, proptosis and ecchymosis were the two most frequent ocular manifestations of neuroblastoma, each observed in 4 (67%) of the 6 cases."
    explanation: >-
      In a population-based cohort of all children resident in Olmsted County,
      Minnesota, who were diagnosed with neuroblastoma from 1969 through 2008, 6
      of the 14 had ocular manifestations, all with orbital metastasis, and
      proptosis was observed in 4 of those 6, so in 4 of the 14 children (4/14 =
      28.6%). This direct count is in the OCCASIONAL band, near its upper edge,
      and is a higher proportion than the Hospital for Sick Children series
      reports for proptosis or periorbital ecchymosis. The authors suggest that
      their high rate of orbital metastasis may reflect advanced disease in
      children diagnosed early in the study period, and none of the children
      with eye findings was diagnosed in its later decades. The cohort is very
      small, and the paper counts eye findings whenever they were seen, not only
      at presentation.
  - reference: PMID:32006485
    reference_title: "Incidence and Prognostic Role of the Ocular Manifestations of Neuroblastoma in Children."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The medical records of patients diagnosed with neuroblastoma between 1989 and 2017 at a tertiary care pediatric hospital were analyzed. ... There were 523 patients with neuroblastoma in the study cohort. ... A total of 86 patients (16.4%) had ocular manifestations of neuroblastoma, 58 at presentation and 29 during the disease course. The most common findings were orbital involvement in 37 (43.0%)"
    explanation: >-
      Retrospective cohort study of 523 patients with neuroblastoma diagnosed
      between 1989 and 2017 at a tertiary care pediatric hospital: orbital
      involvement was recorded in 37 (37/523 = 7.1%), at presentation or during
      the disease course. Orbital metastasis is the cause of proptosis given in
      the Hospital for Sick Children abstract, but this abstract gives no
      proptosis count, so the figure supports the band indirectly. It is the
      most recent series cited here and lies in the OCCASIONAL band, near its
      lower edge.

      In the São Paulo series, a retrospective review of the medical records of

- category: Gastrointestinal
  name: Diarrhea
  frequency: VERY_RARE
  description: >-
    Chronic watery diarrhea caused by tumor secretion of vasoactive intestinal
    peptide (VIP) is a rare paraneoplastic syndrome. VIP-secreting neuroblastic
    tumors are usually associated with differentiation, and the diarrhea is
    relieved by resection of the tumor. VIP secretion can also arise secondarily
    in a high-risk tumor during treatment.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: chronic watery diarrhea
    term:
      id: HP:0005208
      label: Secretory diarrhea
    temporality: CHRONIC
  notes: >-
    Bound to HP:0005208 Secretory diarrhea because tumor vasoactive intestinal
    peptide causes secretory diarrhea; the chronic course is recorded with
    temporality CHRONIC.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40082825
    reference_title: "Chronic diarrhea related to neuroblastoma: the important role of vasoactive intestinal peptide in tumor pathology and survival."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "However, recent studies have updated the typical watery-diarrhea syndrome caused by VIP secretion in NB; this is now considered one of the rare digestive tract-related PNS, accounting for less than 3% of all patients with NB"
    explanation: >-
      The discussion of this single-center study states that the watery-diarrhea
      syndrome caused by tumor VIP secretion accounts for less than 3% of all
      patients with neuroblastoma, which places it in the VERY_RARE band. The
      figure is the authors' summary of the literature, not a proportion
      measured in their own series. The band rests on this summary figure; read
      as an upper bound, a figure below 3% lies within VERY_RARE, which covers
      fewer than 5% of patients. The study's own series was selected by tumor
      resection and is recorded as a separate population context rather than
      used for the band. The figure concerns VIP-driven diarrhea, not diarrhea
      caused by treatment toxicity or by surgery.
  - reference: PMID:40082825
    reference_title: "Chronic diarrhea related to neuroblastoma: the important role of vasoactive intestinal peptide in tumor pathology and survival."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "In the digestive tract, VIP binds to VPAC1 on intestinal epithelial cells, causing secretory diarrhea and ion disturbance"
    explanation: >-
      Background sentence in the introduction: in the digestive tract,
      vasoactive intestinal peptide binds to VPAC1 receptors on intestinal
      epithelial cells and causes secretory diarrhea and ion disturbance. It is
      a statement of general physiology cited from earlier work, not a finding
      of this study, and it supports binding the phenotype to secretory
      diarrhea.
  - reference: PMID:40082825
    reference_title: "Chronic diarrhea related to neuroblastoma: the important role of vasoactive intestinal peptide in tumor pathology and survival."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "All six cases visited hospitals for varying periods (1-12 months) for chronic diarrhea"
    explanation: >-
      In the series of children whose tumors were resected at Shengjing Hospital
      of China Medical University, all six children with refractory watery
      diarrhea had attended hospitals for chronic diarrhea over periods of 1-12
      months, which supports recording the diarrhea as chronic. A child with
      ganglioneuroblastoma, which this series counts as neuroblastoma, was among
      the six. The series was selected by surgery, so it gives no frequency for
      neuroblastoma as a whole.
  - reference: PMID:19143025
    reference_title: "VIP hypersecretion as primary or secondary syndrome in neuroblastoma: A retrospective study by the Société Française des Cancers de l'Enfant (SFCE)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "VIP secreting NTs are usually associated with differentiation; they can also secondarily arise from a high-risk tumor upon treatment."
    explanation: >-
      Conclusion of a retrospective review, by the French pediatric cancer
      society (SFCE), of the French experience of neuroblastic tumors with
      watery diarrhea due to VIP secretion. The authors conclude that
      VIP-secreting neuroblastic tumors are usually associated with
      differentiation, and that VIP-secreting tumors can also arise secondarily
      from a high-risk tumor during treatment. The series covers neuroblastic
      tumors as a group and the abstract does not break the histology down by

      often VIP secretion occurs among neuroblastic tumors.

  description: >-
    Unilateral Horner syndrome is a rare sign, seen mostly with localized
    disease and often with cervical or thoracic tumors; it can be the presenting
    sign.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Horner syndrome
    term:
      id: HP:0002277
      label: Horner syndrome
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:6493702
    reference_title: "Ocular involvement in neuroblastoma: prognostic implications."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "On retrospective review of children seen at the Hospital for Sick Children, ophthalmic involvement was seen in 80 of 405 (20%). ... Unilateral Horner's syndrome occurred in 14 children, as the presenting sign in 9, related to localized disease in 11 and in a favorable location (cervical or thoracic neuroblastoma) in 8."
    explanation: >-
      Retrospective single-center series of children seen at the Hospital for
      Sick Children, from a study of ocular involvement in neuroblastoma. Of the
      405 children, 80 had ophthalmic involvement and 14 had unilateral Horner
      syndrome (14/405 = 3.5%), which places Horner syndrome in the VERY_RARE
      band. The series was not limited to one stage or tumor site, so it is used
      for the overall frequency band. Horner syndrome was the presenting sign in
      9 and was related to localized disease in 11, and in 8 the neuroblastoma
      was cervical or thoracic, a location the authors call favorable. The first
      quoted sentence supplies the 405 denominator. The abstract does not say
      whether the cases in which Horner syndrome was not the presenting sign
      were caused by the tumor or followed surgery.
  - reference: PMID:32006485
    reference_title: "Incidence and Prognostic Role of the Ocular Manifestations of Neuroblastoma in Children."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "There were 523 patients with neuroblastoma in the study cohort. ... A total of 86 patients (16.4%) had ocular manifestations of neuroblastoma, 58 at presentation and 29 during the disease course. The most common findings were ... Horner syndrome in 24 (27.9%). In 16 patients (3.1%), there were only ocular findings at presentation, including ... 7 (1.3%) with Horner syndrome"
    explanation: >-
      Retrospective cohort study of 523 patients with neuroblastoma diagnosed at
      a tertiary care pediatric hospital. Horner syndrome was recorded in 24 of
      the 523 (24/523 = 4.6%), which is within the VERY_RARE band but close to
      its upper limit. The 27.9% in the quote is a share of the 86 patients with
      ocular manifestations, not of the whole cohort, and those 86 include
      manifestations first seen during the disease course, so the count of 24
      covers Horner syndrome at presentation or later. Of the 16 patients whose
      only findings at presentation were ocular, 7 (1.3% of the cohort) had
      Horner syndrome, so it can be the presenting sign on its own. The abstract
      does not give laterality, stage or tumor site for these patients, or say
      whether any case followed surgery.
- category: Neurologic
  name: Spinal Cord Compression
  frequency: OCCASIONAL
  description: >-
    Tumors next to the spine can grow through the intervertebral foramina into
    the spinal canal and compress the spinal cord, causing motor deficit, pain,
    sphincter dysfunction or sensory loss; the adjacent nerve roots can be
    compressed as well.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: spinal cord compression from intraspinal tumor extension
    term:
      id: HP:0002176
      label: Spinal cord compression
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:11134211
    reference_title: "Neuroblastoma with symptomatic spinal cord compression at diagnosis: treatment and results with 76 cases."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Of 1,462 children with neuroblastoma registered between 1979 and 1998, 76 (5.2%) presented with signs/symptoms of SCC, including motor deficit in 75 patients ... pain in 47, sphincteric deficit in 30, and sensory loss in 11."
    explanation: >-
      Of 1,462 children with neuroblastoma registered between 1979 and 1998 in
      this registry series (De Bernardi et al.), 76 (5.2%) presented with signs
      or symptoms of spinal cord compression; the abstract's purpose statement
      defines SCC as spinal cord compression. The denominator is every
      registered child with neuroblastoma rather than a selected subgroup, and
      5.2% falls in the OCCASIONAL band. The deficit counts are within the 76
      children with compression, not the whole series: 75 had a motor deficit,
      47 pain, 30 a sphincteric deficit and 11 sensory loss. Limitations: this
      is a single registry series; it counts only compression with signs or
      symptoms at diagnosis, not intraspinal tumor extension without symptoms;
      and 5.2% is only just above the lower edge of the OCCASIONAL band, next to
      VERY_RARE.
  - reference: PMID:36299690
    reference_title: "Presenting features of neuroblastoma with spinal canal invasion. A prospective study of the International Society of Pediatric Oncology Europe - Neuroblastoma (SIOPEN)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "As NB grows close to the spine, it may infiltrate the intervertebral foramina, invade the spinal canal (SCI) and compress the spinal cord and/or nerve roots"
    explanation: >-
      The introduction of this SIOPEN prospective study of neuroblastoma with
      spinal canal invasion (NB-SCI) states how the phenotype can arise:
      neuroblastoma growing close to the spine may infiltrate the intervertebral
      foramina, invade the spinal canal and compress the spinal cord and/or
      nerve roots. The sentence is background that the authors cite to an
      earlier publication, not a finding of this study, and it is in the
      introduction of the full text rather than in the abstract.
  phenotype_contexts:
  - population: "Children with neuroblastoma and spinal canal invasion in the SIOPEN prospective multinational NB-SCI study (196 evaluable patients)"
    notes: >-
      A cohort selected for spinal canal invasion, which the study defines as
      tumor growth through the neural foramina into the spinal canal, so the
      proportions below are conditional on intraspinal extension, not rates for
      neuroblastoma as a whole. Of the 208 patients registered, 196 were
      evaluable; 67% were symptomatic and 33% asymptomatic at enrollment.
      Symptomatic means any symptom attributed to the spinal canal invasion and
      recorded with standardized measures (motor deficit, pain, sensory deficit,
      bladder or bowel dysfunction, spine deformity or dyspnea), which is
      somewhat broader than signs of cord compression alone, so the symptomatic
      proportion is not recorded as a frequency of spinal cord compression. The
      cohort also includes tumors the authors class as histologically benign
      (ganglioneuroma, intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma) and a few patients
      enrolled at relapse. The asymptomatic share shows that tumor in the spinal
      canal does not always cause clinical compression; such asymptomatic
      extension is not counted in the registry rate given in the phenotype's
      main evidence.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:36299690
      reference_title: "Presenting features of neuroblastoma with spinal canal invasion. A prospective study of the International Society of Pediatric Oncology Europe - Neuroblastoma (SIOPEN)."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Of the 208 NB-SCI patients registered, 196 were evaluable for this analysis of whom 67% were symptomatic and 33% asymptomatic."
      explanation: >-
        In the SIOPEN prospective NB-SCI cohort, 196 of the 208 registered
        patients with neuroblastoma and spinal canal invasion were evaluable,
        and 67% of them were symptomatic while 33% were asymptomatic. The quote
        counts patients with any symptom of spinal canal invasion and does not
        itself name cord compression; reading it as symptomatic compression
        relies on the abstract's background statement that the majority of
        children with neuroblastoma and spinal canal invasion have symptoms of
        epidural compression of the spinal cord and/or spinal nerves, which is
        why it is graded indirect. The cohort was selected for spinal canal
        invasion, so the proportion is not a frequency for neuroblastoma in
        general.
- category: Hematologic
  name: Anemia
  description: >-
    Anemia is one of the commonest general symptoms at presentation. In one
    retrospective series it was significantly associated with heavier
    infiltration of the bone marrow by tumor cells, although two smaller series
    that compared any marrow infiltration with none found it common in both
    groups.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Anemia
    term:
      id: HP:0001903
      label: Anemia
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:6670848
    reference_title: "Neuroblastoma in 88 children. Clinical features, prognostic factors, results and late effects of therapy."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "A retrospective series of 88 patient under 15 with primary neuroblastoma from years 1951-1978 was analyzed. ... On the basis of histological differentiation, the series contained 67 (76.1%) neuroblastomas and 21 (23.9%) ganglioneuroblastomas. ... The commonest general symptoms were anemia (34.1% of all patients), vague pyrexia (25.0%), lack of appetite, weight loss (18.2%) and poor general condition (15.9%)."
    explanation: >-
      In a retrospective series of 88 patients under 15 years of age with
      primary neuroblastoma, admitted between 1951 and 1978, anemia was the
      commonest general symptom, recorded in 34.1% of all patients. On
      histological re-examination the series held 67 neuroblastomas and 21
      ganglioneuroblastomas, and the anemia figure is given for all patients,
      not for the neuroblastomas alone. Ganglioneuroblastoma is a separate
      neuroblastic tumor outside this entry, so no frequency band is set from
      this series; the figure would sit just above the lower edge of the
      Frequent band. All Evans stages, I to IV-S, were represented, but general
      symptoms as a group were commonest in stage III and IV patients, so the
      figure reflects this series' stage mix. Anemia is not defined in the
      abstract (no hemoglobin threshold).
  - reference: PMID:28801367
    reference_title: "Comparison of Hematological Aspects between Neuroblastoma Patients with and without Bone Marrow Infiltration."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Erythrocytopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia were significantly (p<0.05) associated with marrow infiltration of >10% malignant cells."
    explanation: >-
      In a retrospective series comparing blood counts in neuroblastoma patients
      with and without bone marrow infiltration, anemia, together with
      erythrocytopenia and thrombocytopenia, was significantly associated
      (p<0.05) with marrow infiltration by more than 10% malignant cells. This
      is an association in one series, not a frequency: the abstract gives no
      anemia rate or definition, and an association does not show that the
      infiltration causes the anemia.
  phenotype_contexts:
  - population: "Newly diagnosed patients with neuroblastoma referred for staging bone marrow examination, King George Medical University, Lucknow, India (79 patients, 44 with marrow infiltration)"
    notes: >-
      Anemia was present in 81.2% (36/44) of the patients with marrow
      infiltration and was not significantly correlated with infiltration (p =
      0.594). The authors attribute the anemia to the frequency of iron
      insufficiency in India rather than to the disease. No frequency is given
      for this context, because the figure is conditional on marrow
      infiltration.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:37323595
      reference_title: "Study of Hemato-morphological Features in Neuroblastoma Infiltrating Marrow."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "The complete blood count of neuroblastoma cases with marrow infiltration revealed anemia in 81.2% (36/44) of the cases ... All remaining hematological parameters such as anemia ( p = 0.594), leukopenia ( p = 0.189), and bicytopenia ( p = 0.369) were not significantly correlated with marrow infiltration in neuroblastoma cases. ... No significant correlation was noted for anemia in patients of neuroblastoma with and without infiltration, presumably due to the frequency of iron insufficiency in India rather than related to the illness itself."
      explanation: >-
        In this retrospective series of newly diagnosed patients referred for
        staging marrow examination, anemia was found in 81.2% (36/44) of those
        with marrow infiltration and was not significantly correlated with
        infiltration (p = 0.594); the authors suggest iron insufficiency, common
        in India, rather than the disease as the explanation. A referral series

  - population: "Newly diagnosed children with neuroblastoma referred for staging bone marrow examination, Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, India (44 children, 24 with marrow involvement)"
    notes: >-
      Anemia was present in 87.5% of the children with marrow involvement and in
      75% of those without. The authors attribute it to nutritional deficiency
      rather than to marrow infiltration. No frequency is given for this
      context, because the figures are conditional on marrow status.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:25548446
      reference_title: "Bone Marrow Involvement in Neuroblastoma: A Study of Hemato-morphological Features."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Complete blood counts in involved cases showed that anemia was present in 87.5 % cases ... In the uninvolved cases anemia was seen in 75 %, leucopenia in none and thrombocytopenia in 10 % cases. ... Anemia, though was common in both group of patients with and without infiltration, it is thought to be due to nutritional deficiency rather than due to tumor infiltration in marrow."
      explanation: >-

- category: Hepatic
  name: Hepatomegaly
  description: >-
    In infants with INSS stage 4S neuroblastoma, the special metastatic stage of
    infancy in which a localized primary tumor has spread only to the liver,
    skin and/or bone marrow, the liver is the main metastatic site. Hepatomegaly
    and its complications can be fatal in these infants.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Hepatomegaly
    term:
      id: HP:0002240
      label: Hepatomegaly
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30444686
    reference_title: "Defining Risk Factors for Chemotherapeutic Intervention in Infants With Stage 4S Neuroblastoma: A Report From Children's Oncology Group Study ANBL0531."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "five acute deaths were a result of hepatomegaly and associated toxicities"
    explanation: >-
      In the Children's Oncology Group trial ANBL0531, which enrolled infants
      with stage 4S neuroblastoma who had impaired or impending organ
      dysfunction or unfavorable tumor biology and excluded infants whose tumors
      had known MYCN amplification (infants too ill for biopsy could enroll with
      tumor biology unknown), five acute deaths were a result of hepatomegaly
      and associated toxicities. The trial counted deaths from late relapse and
      from treatment complications separately, so the authors attribute these
      deaths to hepatomegaly and its complications rather than to treatment.
      This shows that hepatomegaly can be fatal in stage 4S disease. The trial
      enrolled only a higher-risk subset of stage 4S infants (most infants with
      stage 4S disease do well with observation or minimal chemotherapy), so the
      quote speaks to severity, not to how often hepatomegaly occurs.
  phenotype_contexts:
  - population: "Infants with stage 4s neuroblastoma treated in French Society of Paediatric Oncology centers, 1990-2000 (94 infants)"
    notes: >-
      In this SFOP series, hepatic dissemination was present in 87 of 94 infants
      (92%). This counts liver metastasis rather than measured liver
      enlargement, so no hepatomegaly frequency is given. The series excluded
      infants whose liver involvement came from contiguous spread of a large
      abdominal primary tumor.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:12888814
      reference_title: "Treatment of stage 4s neuroblastoma--report of 10 years' experience of the French Society of Paediatric Oncology (SFOP)."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: "Most tumours showed hepatic dissemination (87 out of 94, 92%), with bone marrow and skin metastasis occurring much less frequently."
      explanation: >-
        In this retrospective review by the French Society of Paediatric
        Oncology (SFOP) of infants with stage 4s neuroblastoma, 87 of 94 (92%)
        had hepatic dissemination, while bone marrow and skin metastases were
        much less frequent, so the liver was the main metastatic site. The paper
        counts liver metastasis, not liver size: it reports no hepatomegaly
        count, and in some infants liver metastases were found only at surgery,
        so liver involvement was not always clinically evident. Hepatomegaly
        follows from this metastatic burden only by inference, so the figure
        supports the phenotype indirectly and is not entered as a hepatomegaly
        frequency. The series did not apply the INSS limit on marrow involvement
        and included infants with bilateral adrenal tumors, which the authors
        note strict INSS staging does not take into account, so its stage 4s
        group is broader than strict INSS stage 4S.

biochemical:
- name: Catecholamine Metabolites
  notes: >-
    Elevated urinary catecholamine metabolites, classically vanillylmandelic
    acid (VMA) and homovanillic acid (HVA), are found in most neuroblastomas
    at diagnosis and support the diagnosis. Reviews cite high urinary
    catecholamine levels in more than 90% of cases (92% for VMA and HVA in
    clinically presenting neuroblastoma), and in a series of patients who
    later relapsed or progressed, urinary VMA and/or HVA had been abnormal at
    diagnosis in 92%. In two diagnostic series published in 2017 and 2020,
    however, the VMA and HVA pair had a diagnostic sensitivity of 82-84%,
    rising to 95% in the 2017 series when all eight urinary metabolites in
    its panel were combined. Relapse or progression cannot be detected
    reliably by monitoring tumor markers alone.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28061374
    reference_title: "Catecholamines profiles at diagnosis: Increased diagnostic sensitivity and correlation with biological and clinical features in neuroblastoma patients."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The combination of the classical markers VMA and HVA had a diagnostic sensitivity of 84%. NMN was the most sensitive single diagnostic metabolite with overall sensitivity of 89%. When all 8 metabolites were combined, a diagnostic sensitivity of 95% was achieved."
    explanation: >-
      In patients at diagnosis, VMA and HVA together had a diagnostic
      sensitivity of 84%, below the classical figure of more than 90%;
      combining all eight urinary metabolites measured raised it to 95%.
      Normetanephrine (NMN) alone reached 89%.
  - reference: PMID:31724812
    reference_title: "Biochemical testing for neuroblastoma using plasma free 3-O-methyldopa, 3-methoxytyramine, and normetanephrine."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Overall, 94 of the 96 patients with neuroblastoma had concentrations of 3-methoxytyramine or normetanephrine above age-specific upper limits of reference intervals, providing a diagnostic sensitivity of 97.9% that was higher (P < 0.0001) than that of 82.2% for HVA and VMA."
    explanation: >-
      A second diagnostic series: urinary HVA and VMA had a diagnostic
      sensitivity of 82.2%, lower than the 97.9% of plasma 3-methoxytyramine
      or normetanephrine. The abstract does not give the denominator for the
      urinary comparison.
  - reference: PMID:8790511
    reference_title: "Screening for neuroblastoma: a review of the evidence."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The screening test consists of measurements of the levels of vanillylmandelic acid and homovanillic acid in the urine; these metabolites of catecholamine are excreted in the urine of 92% of patients with clinically presenting neuroblastoma."
    explanation: >-
      The classical review figure for the VMA and HVA pair: 92% of patients
      with clinically presenting neuroblastoma, stated without a source cohort
      in the abstract.
  - reference: PMID:15235064
    reference_title: "Neuroblastoma: a disease requiring a multitude of imaging studies."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Origin from precursors of the sympathetic nervous system accounts for (a) primary sites in adrenal glands and in paraspinal locations from neck to pelvis and (b) high urinary levels of catecholamines in >90% of cases."
    explanation: >-
      A review statement of high urinary catecholamine levels in more than 90%
      of cases. It refers to urinary catecholamines in general rather than to
      VMA and HVA specifically.
  - reference: PMID:12932669
    reference_title: "Tumour markers are poor predictors for relapse or progression in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "At diagnosis, we found abnormal results in 75% for VMA and/or HVA (s), 92% for VMA and/or HVA (u), 90% for NSE, and 81% for LDH."
    explanation: >-
      In patients who later relapsed or progressed after first-line treatment,
      urinary (u) VMA and/or HVA had been abnormal in 92% at diagnosis (serum
      (s) 75%). The cohort is restricted to patients who relapsed or
      progressed, so it is not an unselected diagnostic series.
  - reference: PMID:12932669
    reference_title: "Tumour markers are poor predictors for relapse or progression in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Relapse or progression in neuroblastoma cannot be detected reliably by monitoring tumour markers alone."
    explanation: >-
      Qualifies the use of these markers in follow-up: in patients who
      relapsed or progressed after first-line treatment, the authors conclude
      that monitoring tumour markers, which in this study included urinary and
      serum VMA and HVA, does not reliably detect relapse or progression on
      its own.
- name: Neuron-Specific Enolase
  presence: INCREASED
  biomarker_term:
    preferred_term: neuron-specific enolase
    term:
      id: NCIT:C62216
      label: Gamma-Enolase
  notes: >-
    Serum neuron-specific enolase (NSE) is raised at diagnosis in most children
    with metastatic (stage IV) neuroblastoma: in a Children's Cancer Study Group
    series of 122 such children, 96% had levels more than three standard
    deviations above the mean for age-matched normal children. In a series of 61
    children with neuroblastoma of all stages, sampled at diagnosis, median
    serum NSE was 13, 23, 40 and 214 ng/ml in stages I, II, III and IV, whereas
    stage IV-S levels (median 40 ng/ml) were significantly lower than stage IV
    levels despite extensive tumor burden, so NSE does not simply track tumor
    burden. In stage III and IV disease in that series, a level above 100 ng/ml
    was associated with poor outcome, and the stage IV series, which shares its
    lead authors, suggested the same for stage IV disease. In a cohort
    restricted to 196 patients who had successfully completed first-line
    treatment and later relapsed or progressed, NSE had been abnormal at
    diagnosis in 90%, but that study's abstract does not say how many of them
    had NSE measured or in which specimen.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:12932669
    reference_title: "Tumour markers are poor predictors for relapse or progression in neuroblastoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We analysed the data of neuroblastoma patients who had successfully completed first-line treatment and had laboratory results available from their initial diagnosis and from relapse/progression (n=196). ... At diagnosis, we found abnormal results in 75% for VMA and/or HVA (s), 92% for VMA and/or HVA (u), 90% for NSE, and 81% for LDH."
    explanation: >-
      In a cohort restricted to 196 patients who had successfully completed
      first-line treatment and had laboratory results from both initial
      diagnosis and relapse or progression, NSE results at diagnosis had been
      abnormal in 90%. Every patient in it went on to relapse or progress, so
